  • Storage modes →
  • Emulator endpoints (health, reset, TLS certificate) →
  • Service reference →

docs.title: Services Overview
docs.text:
Floci-AZ provides emulation for several core Azure services.

Service Endpoint Implementation Status Azure Resource Manager /subscriptions/... + /providers/... ✅ Subscriptions, resource groups, resource/provider listing; management-plane fallthrough for the Microsoft.* providers Blob Storage /{account}/ ✅ Full CRUD; ADLS Gen2 DFS filesystem/path operations with Hadoop ABFS 3.3.4 compatibility; user delegation key/SAS Queue Storage /{account}-queue/ ✅ Full CRUD Azure SignalR Service /server/, /client/, *.service.signalr.net ✅ Default mode over WebSockets; ASP.NET Core hubs, JSON/MessagePack, groups, users, and broadcasts. Per-account isolation through {account}.service.signalr.net hostnames Table Storage /{account}-table/ ✅ Full CRUD Azure Functions /{account}-functions/ ✅ HTTP Triggers, Docker runtimes App Configuration /{account}-appconfig/ ✅ Key-values, labels, feature flags, snapshots, revisions, locks, pagination, $select, tags filtering, Accept-Datetime, Sync-Token Cosmos DB (SQL API) /{account}-cosmos/ ✅ Databases, containers, documents CRUD, SQL queries, partition keys Cosmos DB multi-API (engine sidecars) ✅ MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table, NoSQL (opt-in Docker engines) Key Vault /{account}-keyvault/ ✅ Self-signed certificates with PFX/PEM secrets; secrets & keys CRUD, versioning, soft-delete, properties update, backup/restore, rotation, RSA/EC/oct crypto, /rng, Managed HSM Event Hubs AMQP :5672 / Kafka :9093 ✅ AMQP 1.0 (Artemis), Kafka-compatible (Redpanda, opt-in) Service Bus /{account}-servicebus/ + AMQP :5673 ✅ Queues, topics, subscriptions (dynamic); AMQP 1.0 via Artemis sidecar or mocked Azure SQL Database ARM path + /{account}-sql/ ✅ Servers, databases, firewall rules; ARM-only by default, managed SQL Server opt-in Azure Database for PostgreSQL ARM path (Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL) + /{account}-postgres/ ✅ Flexible servers, databases, firewall rules, configurations; Docker-backed postgres containers or mocked Azure Database for MySQL ARM path (Microsoft.DBforMySQL) + /{account}-mysql/ ✅ Flexible servers, databases, firewall rules, configurations; Docker-backed mysql containers or mocked Azure Database for MariaDB ARM path (Microsoft.DBforMariaDB) + /{account}-mariadb/ ✅ Servers (single-server model), databases, firewall rules, configurations; Docker-backed mariadb containers or mocked Azure Kubernetes Service ARM path (Microsoft.ContainerService) ✅ Clusters, agent pools, credentials; real k3s containers or mocked Azure Container Apps ARM path (Microsoft.App) + FQDN ingress ✅ Managed environments, apps, revisions, ingress, secrets, min/max replicas; Docker-backed or mocked API Management ARM path (Microsoft.ApiManagement) + /{account}-apim/ ✅ APIs, operations, products, subscriptions, named values, backends, OpenAPI import; gateway routing + policy subset Virtual Network ARM path (Microsoft.Network) ✅ VNets, subnets, NICs, public IPs, NSGs, private DNS zones (+ virtual network links, record sets), private endpoints (+ private DNS zone groups), private link services; in-process ARM state for Terraform/OpenTofu and VM dependencies Virtual Machines ARM path (Microsoft.Compute) ✅ VM lifecycle (create/start/stop/deallocate/restart/delete/list), instanceView; mocked by default, optional container-backed mode (mocked: false) Azure Cache for Redis ARM path (Microsoft.Cache) ✅ Cache CRUD, listKeys/regenerateKey; real Redis containers (data plane) or mocked Azure Container Registry ARM path (Microsoft.ContainerRegistry) ✅ Registry CRUD, admin credentials, checkNameAvailability; az acr login via the Entra token exchange on {name}.azurecr.io; one shared registry:2 (Docker Registry V2 push/pull) or mocked Azure Container Instances ARM path (Microsoft.ContainerInstance) ✅ Container group lifecycle (create/update/delete/list), start/stop/restart, container logs, instanceView; real Docker containers (shared-netns pods) or mocked Microsoft Entra ID /{tenant}/oauth2/... + /.well-known/openid-configuration ✅ OpenID Connect provider: RS256-signed tokens, JWKS, discovery; client-credentials, ROPC, and authorization-code+PKCE grants; scoped OIDC UserInfo; app registrations managed through Microsoft Graph Microsoft Graph /v1.0/... ✅ Narrow slice: service principal discovery, group-membership management (getMemberGroups, members/$ref), app registrations with client secrets (applications, addPassword / removePassword); full Graph CRUD out of scope Event Grid ARM path (Microsoft.EventGrid) + /{topic}-eventgrid/api/events ✅ Custom Topics, access keys, webhook event subscriptions with filters, publish (Event Grid + CloudEvents 1.0), async delivery with retry, subscription validation handshake Azure Monitor / Log Analytics ARM path (Microsoft.OperationalInsights / Microsoft.Insights) + /dataCollectionRules/... + /v1/workspaces/... ✅ Workspaces, Data Collection Endpoints/Rules; Logs Ingestion API; Log Analytics query with a KQL subset (where/project/take/limit, timespan); subscription Activity Log (Administrative entries for every ARM write, delete and action, $filter / $select / paging) Communication Services Email /emails:send + /emailMessages + ARM path (Microsoft.Communication) ✅ ACS Email send + status polling; in-memory inspection mailbox (Mailpit-style); ARM communication/email services + domains. No real delivery Managed Identity ARM path (Microsoft.ManagedIdentity) + /metadata/identity/oauth2/token + /msi/token ✅ User-assigned identities + federated identity credentials, system-assigned identities/default, IMDS token endpoint (ManagedIdentityCredential via AZURE_POD_IDENTITY_AUTHORITY_HOST), App Service token endpoint (IDENTITY_ENDPOINT / IDENTITY_HEADER); tokens signed with the Entra key ARM Template Deployments ARM path (Microsoft.Resources/deployments) ✅ Resource-group and subscription template deployments run asynchronously through the real handlers: parameters, variables, dependsOn and implicit reference() ordering, outputs read live, validate, exportTemplate, copy loops, nested deployments (Bicep modules), linked templates (templateLink, parametersLink, relativePath) Azure Policy ARM path (Microsoft.Authorization/policy*) ✅ Policy definitions, set definitions, assignments and exemptions at management-group, subscription, resource-group and resource scope; assigned rules evaluated on writes (deny, append, audit); compliance states, summaries and on-demand scans through Microsoft.PolicyInsights; no built-in definitions Azure Resource Graph ARM path (Microsoft.ResourceGraph/resources) ✅ KQL queries over resources, resourcecontainers and policyresources: where, extend, project, summarize, order by, distinct, union, join, the comparison and string operators, the conversion and string functions; objectArray / table formats, $top / $skip / $skipToken paging Azure Management Groups ARM path (Microsoft.Management/managementGroups) ✅ Tenant root group, groups (create, get with $expand / $recurse, patch, delete, list, descendants), subscription membership, getEntities, checkNameAvailability

docs.title: Unified Endpoint
docs.text: All services are accessible through a single port (4577). The routing is handled by inspecting the request path and headers.

docs.title: Docker-backed services
docs.text:
The following services spin up Docker containers on demand and require the Docker socket:

Service Docker image Data plane Azure Functions User-provided image HTTP to container Azure SQL Database mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest Optional managed mode; TDS direct to container port Cosmos DB engines Various (mongo, postgres, cassandra, …) Protocol direct to container port Azure Kubernetes Service rancher/k3s:latest kubectl direct to k3s API server port Azure Database for PostgreSQL postgres:17-alpine PostgreSQL wire protocol direct to container port Azure Database for MySQL mysql:8.0 MySQL wire protocol direct to container port Azure Database for MariaDB mariadb:10.11 MySQL wire protocol direct to container port Azure Container Apps User-provided images HTTP ingress proxied through port 4577 Azure Container Instances User-provided images Shared-netns group, published ports on 7500-7599 (opt in with mocked: false) Virtual Machines storageProfile.imageReference, falling back to ubuntu:22.04 One keep-alive Linux container per VM (opt in with mocked: false)

These services must have access to the Docker daemon (/var/run/docker.sock mount in Docker Compose).

docs.title: Azure Container Instances (ACI)
docs.text:
Compatible with the azure-mgmt-containerinstance SDK, the az container CLI, Terraform's azurerm_container_group, and any ARM-speaking client.

Mocked mode (default): no Docker required. Container groups are emulated as pure ARM control-plane resources: they provision instantly with a synthetic IP and report a Running instance view.

Container-backed mode: set FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACI_MOCKED=false to back each container group with real Docker containers. Group members share a network namespace (localhost between containers, like real ACI), published ports are mapped onto the host (preferring the container port itself, falling back to the configured range), logs returns the real container output (honoring tail and timestamps), and instanceView reports the real Docker state (Running / Terminated with exit code / Waiting). Groups provision asynchronously (Creating → Succeeded once every container runs, or an honest Failed when Docker cannot start them).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Lifecycle: CreateOrUpdate, Get, Delete, List (by subscription and by resource group), UpdateTags
  • Actions: start, stop, restart with the spec's exact LRO shapes (Location-header polling); in container-backed mode they map onto the backing containers (the netns-owning primary restarts first, then the secondaries)
  • Container logs: GET .../containers/{name}/logs?tail=&timestamps= (real Docker logs in container-backed mode, empty in mocked mode)
  • Pod semantics: multi-container groups share one network namespace: the first container owns the network and the published ports; the rest join it and reach each other on localhost
  • Volumes: emptyDir (named Docker volume) and secret (files injected before start)
  • instanceView: group state plus per-container currentState/restartCount on single GETs (list responses omit it, matching the spec's list model); real Docker state when unmocked
  • Terraform-safe read-backs: container ports and resources.requests are always present (server defaults cpu: 1.0, memoryInGB: 1.5 when omitted, matching the az CLI's behaviour), and enum casing is normalized to canonical Azure values (Linux, Always, TCP, Public)
  • Secret hygiene: secureValue environment variables, imageRegistryCredentials passwords, and secret-volume contents are accepted but never echoed back
  • Resource index: groups appear in GET .../resourceGroups/{rg}/resources, so terraform destroy sees them before removing a resource group

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
All operations use ARM paths:

PUT    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups/{name}
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups/{name}
PATCH  /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups/{name}
DELETE /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups/{name}
POST   .../containerGroups/{name}/{start|stop|restart}
GET    .../containerGroups/{name}/containers/{container}/logs?tail=&timestamps=
GET    .../containerGroups/{name}/outboundNetworkDependenciesEndpoints
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/locations/{loc}/{cachedImages|capabilities|usages}

docs.title: 1: Create a container group
docs.text:
curl -s -X PUT \
  "http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/my-sub/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups/my-app?api-version=2023-05-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "location": "eastus",
    "properties": {
      "containers": [
        {
          "name": "web",
          "properties": {
            "image": "hashicorp/http-echo:latest",
            "command": ["/http-echo", "-text=hello"],
            "ports": [{"port": 5678}],
            "resources": {"requests": {"cpu": 0.5, "memoryInGB": 0.5}}
          }
        }
      ],
      "osType": "Linux",
      "ipAddress": {"type": "Public", "ports": [{"port": 5678}], "dnsNameLabel": "my-app"}
    }
  }'

The group is returned with properties.provisioningState = "Succeeded", an IP, and fqdn = "my-app.eastus.azurecontainer.io".

docs.title: 2: Read logs and state
docs.text:
BASE="http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/my-sub/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups/my-app"
curl -s "$BASE?api-version=2023-05-01"                              # full resource + instanceView
curl -s "$BASE/containers/web/logs?api-version=2023-05-01"          # {"content": "..."}

docs.title: 3: Actions
docs.text:
curl -si -X POST "$BASE/stop?api-version=2023-05-01"      # 204, synchronous
curl -si -X POST "$BASE/start?api-version=2023-05-01"     # 202 + Location (poll -> Succeeded)
curl -si -X POST "$BASE/restart?api-version=2023-05-01"   # 204 + Location

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    aci:
      enabled: true
      mocked: true              # true = no Docker, pure ARM state. false = container-backed
      base-port: 7500           # host-port range for published group ports
      max-port: 7599
Env var Default Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACI_ENABLED true Enable/disable the service FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACI_MOCKED true Mocked mode (no Docker); false backs each group with real Docker containers FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACI_BASE_PORT 7500 Start of the host port range for published ports (container-backed mode only) FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACI_MAX_PORT 7599 End of the host port range (container-backed mode only)

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• exec and attach return an honest 501: they hand out a live websocket in real Azure, which the emulator does not provide.
  • azureFile and gitRepo volumes are rejected with a 400; emptyDir and secret volumes are supported.
  • Liveness/readiness probes, identity, diagnostics, dnsConfig, subnetIds, GPU resources, and confidential/spot SKUs are stored and echoed but not enforced. CPU requests are stored but not enforced as a Docker limit (memory requests are).
  • restartPolicy is stored and echoed but not mapped onto Docker restart policies: an exited container stays Terminated in the instance view.
  • containerGroupProfiles and ngroups (2025-09-01 additions) are not implemented.
  • The ipAddress.fqdn is cosmetic: nothing resolves *.azurecontainer.io locally.
  • Secondary (non-first) containers cannot resolve emulated hostnames: Docker rejects DNS options in the shared-netns mode they use, so floci-az's embedded DNS is only injected into the primary.
  • command replaces the image's entrypoint (real ACI semantics), not just its CMD.
  • When floci-az itself runs inside Docker, images referencing the emulated ACR's loginServer (floci-az-acr-registry:5000/...) cannot be pulled by the host daemon: pull from the emulated ACR works natively only.
  • Mocked mode reports every container as Running without running anything; use container-backed mode for real state.

docs.title: Azure Container Registry
docs.text: Compatible with the azure-mgmt-containerregistry SDK, the az acr CLI, Terraform's azurerm_container_registry, and any ARM-speaking client for the management plane, plus any standard Docker client (docker login / push / pull, OCI tooling) for the data plane, either anonymously on the registry container's published port or with an Entra token on {name}.azurecr.io.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Registry lifecycle: create, get, update, delete; list by resource group and by subscription
  • Admin credentials: listCredentials / regenerateCredential (username + two passwords)
  • Name availability: checkNameAvailability
  • Usages: listUsages (static quota report)
  • Entra token exchange: the bearer challenge on GET /v2/ and on the /acr/v1/ metadata API, POST /oauth2/exchange and /oauth2/token, so az acr login and the Azure SDK container-registry clients work
  • Repository catalog: GET /acr/v1/_catalog, which the SDK clients' listRepositoryNames calls, lists the same repositories as /v2/_catalog
  • Data plane: a single shared registry:2 sidecar exposing the Docker Registry HTTP API V2 (/v2/…), so images push and pull with the standard Docker client. All registries are backed by one container and isolated by an internal repository prefix ({registryName}/{repo})

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
Management plane (ARM) goes through port 4577:

PUT|GET|PATCH|DELETE  /subscriptions/{s}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/{name}
POST                  .../registries/{name}/listCredentials | regenerateCredential | importImage
GET                   .../registries/{name}/listUsages
POST                  /subscriptions/{s}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/checkNameAvailability

A registry name is a global DNS name: the first subscription to create it owns it, and another subscription's create is 409 AlreadyInUse until the owner deletes it. In Azure each cloud has its own zone (azurecr.us, azurecr.cn), but floci-az serves every registry on {name}.azurecr.io from one shared backing registry, so a name is unique across every configured cloud, not per cloud. checkNameAvailability answers from the same ownership. Paths that differ only in case address the same registry. With parity-overrides.strict-names a name outside 5 to 50 letters and digits is refused with 400 InvalidResourceName (see ARM name syntax).

The data plane has two surfaces onto the same storage.

The registry container's published port is the zero-configuration one. It is plain HTTP, anonymous, and Docker treats localhost:PORT as insecure automatically, so nothing has to be configured:

localhost:5000/{registryName}/{repo}

The port comes from the base-port-max-port range below and is allocated when the shared container starts, on the first registry you create. It is 5000 unless that port is taken, and because loginServer names the Azure host it cannot carry the port, so the registry resource reports it as properties.localPort:

az acr show -n myregistry -g my-rg --query properties.localPort   # 5000

This is a floci-az convenience field, not part of the real ARM contract, and it is the same field PostgreSQL and MySQL servers use to report the port their container published. It is absent in mocked mode, where no container runs. The emulator also logs the port at startup, and docker port floci-az-acr-registry 5000 reports it:

INFO  [io.flo.az.ser.acr.AcrRegistryManager] Started shared ACR registry floci-az-acr-registry on host port 5000

{name}.azurecr.io is what loginServer reports and what Azure-native clients use. It is served by floci-az on 443 when TLS is on (FLOCI_AZ_TLS_ENABLED=true), and carries the endpoints those clients need:

GET       {name}.azurecr.io/v2/                 bearer challenge
POST      {name}.azurecr.io/oauth2/exchange     Entra access token → ACR refresh token
GET|POST  {name}.azurecr.io/oauth2/token        ACR refresh token → scoped access token
*         {name}.azurecr.io/v2/**               Docker Registry HTTP API V2
GET       {name}.azurecr.io/acr/v1/_catalog     repository catalog (ACR metadata API)

The registry name is not part of a repository reference here: {name}.azurecr.io/app is the repository app, exactly as in Azure. floci-az adds the {registryName}/ prefix internally when it proxies to the shared container, and strips it again from upload Location headers, tags/list and _catalog.

Name resolution is required. {name}.azurecr.io must resolve to floci-az, the same requirement *.vault.azure.net already carries for Key Vault. Add a hosts entry (or point your resolver at the emulator) and trust the emulator's certificate, which carries *.azurecr.io:

echo "127.0.0.1 myregistry.azurecr.io" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts
curl -s http://localhost:4577/_floci/tls-cert -o floci-az.crt   # then trust it

Docker needs the certificate in /etc/docker/certs.d/myregistry.azurecr.io/ca.crt. Without name resolution, use the published port instead: it needs none of this.

A hosts entry points one name at the emulator, but a wildcard resolver points all of them, so floci-az serves {name}.azurecr.io only for a registry that was actually created. A name with no registry behind it answers 404 NAME_UNKNOWN at every endpoint, challenge and token included, rather than minting tokens for something that does not exist.

TLS is off by default. The challenge realm carries the scheme the request arrived with (honouring X-Forwarded-Proto behind a terminating proxy), so the token flow is exercisable over plain HTTP, but az acr login and Docker both address a named registry as https:// and need TLS on.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
az acr login and the SDK container-registry clients perform Azure's Entra token exchange rather than a Docker login: GET /v2/ answers 401 with a Bearer challenge naming the realm and service, an Entra access token is traded for a registry refresh token at /oauth2/exchange, and that refresh token is traded for a scoped access token at /oauth2/token. Docker then logs in with the username 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 and the access token as the password. floci-az serves all of it, in both mocked modes.

The Azure SDK container-registry clients (Java, Python, .NET) work the other way round: they send each request without credentials and authenticate only when it is challenged, and only when that challenge carries a scope as well as the service. A request under /acr/v1/ that carries no Authorization header is therefore answered with a challenge naming the scope it needs: registry:catalog:* for /acr/v1/_catalog, and repository:{name}:metadata_read, metadata_write or delete for a repository's metadata, by method. The GET /v2/ ping names no resource, so its challenge carries no scope, as az acr login expects.

Intentional deviations, all of them a consequence of the emulator's existing stance that ARM and Shared Key credentials are accepted without verification:

  • Tokens are issued, not verified. Both tokens are real RS256 JWTs signed by the emulator's Entra signing key, so clients that decode them keep working (the Azure CLI reads the access token's access claim). Nothing checks the Entra token presented at /oauth2/exchange, and nothing checks the refresh token presented at /oauth2/token.
  • No authorization is enforced. The requested scope is recorded in the access token's access claim and then ignored: any token, and any identity, reaches every repository. Only GET /v2/ and the /acr/v1/ metadata API challenge; Docker Registry repository paths under /v2/ are served whether or not a token is presented. Of the metadata API only /acr/v1/_catalog is served; its other paths answer 404 NAME_UNKNOWN once authenticated. Admin credentials are accepted at the token endpoint so the password grant is truthful, but they are not required.
  • The shared backing registry runs anonymous (mirroring the AWS ECR design in the sibling emulator), so its published port serves push and pull with no credentials at all.

Real ACR enforces per-registry auth and repository-scoped permissions; reproducing that on a single shared registry is out of scope.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Anonymous, through the published port. 5000 below is the first free port in the configured range, so substitute the one the startup log reports (Started shared ACR registry ... on host port):

docker tag busybox localhost:5000/myregistry/demo/busybox:v1
docker push localhost:5000/myregistry/demo/busybox:v1
curl http://localhost:5000/v2/_catalog     # {"repositories":["myregistry/demo/busybox", ...]}
docker pull localhost:5000/myregistry/demo/busybox:v1

The same image, through the Azure login server (hosts entry and trusted certificate in place):

az acr create -n myregistry -g my-rg --sku Basic     # loginServer: myregistry.azurecr.io
az acr login -n myregistry
docker tag busybox myregistry.azurecr.io/demo/busybox:v1
docker push myregistry.azurecr.io/demo/busybox:v1
docker pull myregistry.azurecr.io/demo/busybox:v1

az acr login --expose-token returns the refresh token without needing a Docker daemon.

In mocked mode (no Docker) the management plane and the whole auth surface still work; repository operations answer with the registry's UNSUPPORTED error, since no container is running.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    acr:
      enabled: true
      mocked: false             # false (default) = one shared registry:2 for all registries. true = management plane only, no Docker
      default-image: "registry:2"
      base-port: 5000           # host port range start for registry containers
      max-port: 5099            # host port range end
Env var Default Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACR_ENABLED true Enable/disable the service FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACR_MOCKED false Mocked mode (management plane only, no Docker) FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACR_DEFAULT_IMAGE registry:2 Registry container image FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACR_BASE_PORT 5000 Host port range start FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ACR_MAX_PORT 5099 Host port range end

docs.title: Out of scope (future work)
docs.text:
• Token signature verification, repository-level authorization and scope enforcement.
  • Scope maps and tokens as ACR resources, content trust, quarantine, anonymous pull configuration.
  • importImage actual layer copy (accepted as a 202 no-op).
  • Geo-replication, webhooks, ACR Tasks, private link, retention policies (accepted and echoed as static properties, not enforced).
  • SKU behavioral differences (Basic/Standard/Premium accepted; no functional difference).

docs.title: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
docs.text:
Compatible with the azure-mgmt-containerservice SDK, the az aks CLI, Terraform's azurerm_kubernetes_cluster, and any ARM-speaking client.

Requires Docker (in real mode): each AKS cluster maps to one rancher/k3s container. Set FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_MOCKED=true for a lightweight mock that skips Docker entirely.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Clusters: CreateOrUpdate, Get, Delete, List (by subscription and by resource group), UpdateTags
  • Agent pools: List, Get, CreateOrUpdate, Delete
  • Credentials: listClusterAdminCredential, listClusterUserCredential return a base64-encoded kubeconfig
  • Real k3s mode: a privileged k3s container starts per cluster; kubeconfig with real CA is extracted and returned
  • Mocked mode: clusters transition immediately to Succeeded with a synthetic kubeconfig; no Docker required
  • instanceId-based naming: each cluster gets an 8-char UUID prefix, preventing container name collisions across resource groups

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
All operations use ARM paths:

PUT    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/{name}
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/{name}
DELETE /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/{name}
PATCH  /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/{name}
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters
POST   .../managedClusters/{name}/listClusterAdminCredential
POST   .../managedClusters/{name}/listClusterUserCredential
GET    .../managedClusters/{name}/agentPools
GET    .../managedClusters/{name}/agentPools/{poolName}
PUT    .../managedClusters/{name}/agentPools/{poolName}
DELETE .../managedClusters/{name}/agentPools/{poolName}

docs.title: 1: Create a cluster
docs.text:
curl -s -X PUT \
  "http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/my-sub/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/my-cluster?api-version=2024-04-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "location": "eastus",
    "properties": {
      "kubernetesVersion": "1.29",
      "dnsPrefix": "my-cluster-dns",
      "agentPoolProfiles": [
        {
          "name": "nodepool1",
          "count": 1,
          "vmSize": "Standard_DS2_v2",
          "osType": "Linux",
          "mode": "System"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'

In real mode, provisioningState is "Creating" until k3s is ready (30–90 s). Poll with GET until "Succeeded". In mocked mode, the response immediately shows "Succeeded".

docs.title: 2: Poll until ready (real mode only)
docs.text:
while true; do
  STATE=$(curl -s "http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/my-sub/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/my-cluster?api-version=2024-04-01" \
          | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['properties']['provisioningState'])")
  echo "provisioningState: $STATE"
  [ "$STATE" = "Succeeded" ] && break
  sleep 5
done

docs.title: 3: Get the kubeconfig
docs.text:
KUBECONFIG_B64=$(curl -s -X POST \
  "http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/my-sub/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/my-cluster/listClusterAdminCredential?api-version=2024-04-01" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['kubeconfigs'][0]['value'])")

echo "$KUBECONFIG_B64" | base64 -d > ~/.kube/my-cluster.yaml
kubectl --kubeconfig ~/.kube/my-cluster.yaml get nodes

In real mode the kubeconfig points to the live k3s API server. In mocked mode it points to https://localhost:6443 with insecure-skip-tls-verify: true.

In real mode the credential operations answer 409 OperationNotAllowed until the cluster reaches Succeeded and its kubeconfig has been extracted from k3s (for example while it is Creating, or after it Failed), rather than returning a kubeconfig that cannot reach a server.

docs.title: 4: Delete the cluster
docs.text:
curl -s -X DELETE \
  "http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/my-sub/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters/my-cluster?api-version=2024-04-01"
# returns 202 Accepted; the k3s container and its volume are removed immediately

docs.title: SDK Integration
Real vs Mocked Mode
docs.text: Real mode (mocked=false) Mocked mode (mocked=true) Docker required Yes No provisioningState after create Creating → polled to Succeeded Immediately Succeeded Kubeconfig Extracted from k3s: real CA, real server URL Synthetic: insecure-skip-tls-verify: true kubectl connectivity Yes, points at live k3s API server No: k3s not running Container floci-az-aks-{instanceId} (privileged k3s) None Use case Local development, integration tests Unit tests, CI without Docker

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    aks:
      enabled: true
      mocked: false             # true = no Docker; false = real k3s (default)
      default-image: "rancher/k3s:latest"
      api-server-base-port: 6443
      api-server-max-port: 7443
      keep-running-on-shutdown: false
Environment Variable Default Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_ENABLED true Enable or disable the AKS service FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_MOCKED false true = skip Docker, synthetic kubeconfig FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_DEFAULT_IMAGE rancher/k3s:latest k3s Docker image FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_API_SERVER_BASE_PORT 6443 Start of host port range for k3s API servers FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_API_SERVER_MAX_PORT 7443 End of host port range for k3s API servers FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_KEEP_RUNNING_ON_SHUTDOWN false Leave k3s containers running when floci-az stops. Deleting a cluster always removes its container and volume

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
services:
  floci-az:
    image: floci/floci-az:latest
    ports:
      - "4577:4577"
      - "6443-6450:6443-6450"   # k3s API server ports (one per cluster)
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock   # required for real k3s mode
    environment:
      FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_AKS_MOCKED: "false"
      # k3s containers bind to host ports 6443–7443 via Docker daemon.
      # Publish the range you need above.

Sidecar ports: k3s containers bind a host port in the 6443–7443 range directly via the Docker daemon. Publish the port range on the floci-az service if your application needs to reach the k3s API server from outside Docker.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Your App                                                    │
│                                                              │
│  ARM REST calls ──────► floci-az :4577 ──► AksHandler        │
│  (create cluster,                         (state, routing)   │
│   list clusters,                                             │
│   get credentials)                                           │
│                                                              │
│  kubectl / k8s client ────────────────────────────────────►  │
│                               k3s container :6443            │
│                               (floci-az-aks-{instanceId})    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The management plane (ARM API) goes through floci-az on port 4577. The data plane (kubectl, Kubernetes API) connects directly to the k3s container on its allocated port: floci-az is not in the data path.

docs.title: API Management
docs.text: floci-az includes an in-process API Management emulator intended for local development, SDK compatibility tests, and CI workflows that need APIM-shaped ARM resources plus a lightweight gateway. It is not a full Azure APIM gateway implementation: no sidecar is started; everything runs in-process.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Plane Path Management (ARM) Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/... Gateway /{account}-apim/{serviceName}/{apiPath...}, e.g. http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-apim/{serviceName}/...

docs.title: Supported
docs.text:
• Management service resources: create, get, list (by resource group and across the subscription), delete, and checkNameAvailability.
  • API resources: create, get, list, delete.
  • Operation resources: create, get, list, delete.
  • Policy resources at service, API, and operation scope.
  • Product resources and product-to-API links.
  • Subscription resources with gateway subscription-key enforcement.
  • Named values, including secret named values whose properties.value is not exposed in ARM responses.
  • Backends and <set-backend-service backend-id="...">.
  • OpenAPI JSON import for APIs (operation generation from paths); reimport replaces previously generated operations.
  • Gateway routing for API paths and operation URL templates, with backend proxying when an API serviceUrl or backend policy is configured.

docs.title: Gateway requests to an API without a backend
docs.text:
When the matched API has no serviceUrl, no <set-backend-service> policy applies and no <return-response> policy answers the request, the gateway responds with 500 and a JSON error body:

{"error": {"code": "BackendNotConfigured", "message": "API 'catalog-api' in service 'my-apim' has no backend: ..."}}

This status and body are an emulator choice: the response real API Management returns in this case is not covered by the references floci-az is checked against. To mock an API without a backend, configure a <return-response> policy, which is the Azure way to answer from the gateway itself.

docs.title: Supported policy subset
docs.text:
The policy engine intentionally supports a focused subset:

  • <set-header> with exists-action="override" | skip | append | delete
  • <set-query-parameter> with exists-action="override" | skip | delete
  • <rewrite-uri template="...">
  • <set-backend-service base-url="..."> and <set-backend-service backend-id="...">
  • <return-response> with nested <set-status code="..."> and <set-body>
  • Named-value interpolation with {{name}} in supported policy values

docs.title: Service names
docs.text:
A service name is a global DNS name ({name}.azure-api.net, azure-api.us in Azure US Government, azure-api.cn in Azure China): the first subscription and resource group to create it own it, and a create of the same name from any other scope is refused with 409 ServiceAlreadyExists until the owner deletes it. Another scope reads the name as 404, and its DELETE is a no-op 200 that leaves the owner's service in place. The name is unique across every cloud the emulator serves, since one gateway serves every service by name. POST /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/checkNameAvailability answers from the same owners, in any subscription: nameAvailable: false with reason AlreadyExists for an owned name, Invalid for a name outside the service name rule below, and otherwise nameAvailable: true with reason Valid. Paths that differ only in case address the same service and its child resources. With parity-overrides.strict-names a name outside 1 to 50 letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and ending with a letter or digit, is refused with 400 InvalidResourceName (see ARM name syntax).

Services are kept through the storage layer under the store name apim, so they follow the global storage.mode. Their child resources (APIs, operations, policies, products, subscriptions, named values and backends) are still kept in memory only, so under a persistent mode a restart keeps the services but not their children.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    apim:
      enabled: true
Variable Default Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_APIM_ENABLED true Enable/disable the service

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• The full Azure policy language (only the subset above is interpreted)
  • Developer portal, products workflow approvals, and analytics
  • Self-hosted gateways, multi-region deployment, and custom domains
  • Rate-limiting/quota, JWT validation, and caching policies

docs.title: App Configuration
docs.text: Compatible with azure-appconfiguration SDKs (Java, Python, JavaScript, .NET).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Key-values: set, get, delete, list with key/label filters
  • Labels: independent values per (key, label) pair; list distinct labels
  • Feature flags: first-class support via .appconfig.featureflag/ prefix and application/vnd.microsoft.appconfig.ff+json content-type
  • Revisions: full revision history on every write; queryable via GET /revisions
  • Locks: lock/unlock individual key-values to prevent modification
  • Snapshots: point-in-time frozen copies of filtered key-value sets; async provisioning + archive/recover lifecycle
  • ETags: conditional reads (If-None-Match) and conditional writes/deletes (If-Match)
  • Composition types: key (deduplicate by key) and key_label (keep all key+label pairs)
  • Pagination: @nextLink / Link header with opaque after continuation tokens (100 items per page)
  • $select projection: return only requested fields (key, value, content_type, tags, …)
  • Tags filtering: tags=name=value (repeatable, AND semantics) on key-value and revision lists
  • Time-travel: Accept-Datetime returns the historical value/list as of a point in time
  • Sync-Token: consistency token returned on every response

docs.title: Filtering, pagination & consistency
docs.text:
These behaviors are exercised transparently by the SDKs: the notes below describe the wire behavior.

  • Pagination. Lists return at most 100 items. When more exist the response body carries a relative @nextLink (/kv?api-version=2024-09-01&...&after=<token>) and a matching Link: <...>; rel="next" header. The continuation is an opaque base64 after token; SDK pagers follow it automatically.
  • $select. Pass $Select=key,value (CSV) to project each item down to the requested fields.
  • Tags filtering. Repeat tags=env=prod&tags=tier=web to filter key-values/revisions by all given tags (AND). Available on GET /kv and GET /revisions.
  • Accept-Datetime. Send an HTTP-date (or ISO-8601) to read the state as of that moment; resolved from the revision history. Note real clients send this at whole-second resolution.
  • Sync-Token. Every response includes a Sync-Token header (<id>=<base64>;sn=<seq>, monotonic per account). The SDK round-trips it to guarantee read-your-writes consistency within a sequence.

docs.title: Async snapshot provisioning
docs.text:
PUT /snapshots/{name} returns 201 with status: provisioning and an Operation-Location header. SDK pollers (begin_create_snapshot / beginCreateSnapshot) poll GET /operations?snapshot={name}, which reports Succeeded and flips the snapshot to ready. Provisioning is effectively instantaneous in the emulator.

Out of scope (future work)

Dedicated Check* HEAD operations with full header parity, problem+json bodies on every non-404 error path, snapshot retention/expiry enforcement, and the OAuth (AAD) auth flow.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
http://localhost:4577/{accountName}-appconfig

Default account: devstoreaccount1 Default endpoint: http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-appconfig

docs.title: Connection String
docs.text:
The App Configuration SDK expects an HTTPS endpoint. Use the forced-HTTP pattern below for local development:

JavaPythonJavaScript / TypeScript 
import com.azure.data.appconfiguration.ConfigurationClientBuilder;
import com.azure.core.http.policy.HttpPipelinePolicy;
import com.azure.core.http.HttpPipelineCallContext;
import com.azure.core.http.HttpPipelineNextPolicy;
import com.azure.core.http.HttpResponse;
import com.azure.core.util.Context;
import reactor.core.publisher.Mono;
import java.net.URL;

// Rewrite https → http for local emulator
static class ForceHttpPolicy implements HttpPipelinePolicy {
    @Override
    public Mono<HttpResponse> process(HttpPipelineCallContext ctx, HttpPipelineNextPolicy next) {
        try {
            URL url = new URL(ctx.getHttpRequest().getUrl().toString());
            ctx.getHttpRequest().setUrl(new URL("http", url.getHost(), url.getPort(), url.getFile()).toString());
        } catch (Exception ignored) {}
        return next.process();
    }
}

String account  = "devstoreaccount1";
String endpoint = "https://localhost:4577/" + account + "-appconfig";
String connStr  = "Endpoint=" + endpoint + ";Id=" + account + ";Secret=placeholder";

ConfigurationClient client = new ConfigurationClientBuilder()
        .connectionString(connStr)
        .addPolicy(new ForceHttpPolicy())
        .buildClient();

from azure.appconfiguration import AzureAppConfigurationClient
from azure.core.pipeline.transport import RequestsTransport

class ForceHttpTransport(RequestsTransport):
    def send(self, request, **kwargs):
        request.url = request.url.replace("https://", "http://", 1)
        return super().send(request, **kwargs)

account  = "devstoreaccount1"
endpoint = f"https://localhost:4577/{account}-appconfig"
conn_str = f"Endpoint={endpoint};Id={account};Secret=placeholder"

client = AzureAppConfigurationClient.from_connection_string(
    conn_str, transport=ForceHttpTransport()
)

import { AppConfigurationClient } from "@azure/app-configuration";

const account  = "devstoreaccount1";
const endpoint = `https://localhost:4577/${account}-appconfig`;
const connStr  = `Endpoint=${endpoint};Id=${account};Secret=placeholder`;

const client = new AppConfigurationClient(connStr);

List key-values

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
Labels let you maintain environment-specific variants of the same key:

JavaPython 
client.setConfigurationSetting(
    new ConfigurationSetting().setKey("timeout").setValue("30").setLabel("prod"));
client.setConfigurationSetting(
    new ConfigurationSetting().setKey("timeout").setValue("5").setLabel("dev"));

// Fetch by label
String prodVal = client.getConfigurationSetting("timeout", "prod").getValue(); // "30"
String devVal  = client.getConfigurationSetting("timeout", "dev").getValue();  // "5"

client.set_configuration_setting(ConfigurationSetting(key="timeout", value="30", label="prod"))
client.set_configuration_setting(ConfigurationSetting(key="timeout", value="5",  label="dev"))

prod = client.get_configuration_setting("timeout", label_filter="prod").value  # "30"
dev  = client.get_configuration_setting("timeout", label_filter="dev").value   # "5"

docs.title: Feature Flags
Snapshots
docs.text: Snapshots capture a frozen, point-in-time copy of filtered key-values. They are immutable after creation: changes to live key-values do not affect an existing snapshot.

docs.title: Create a snapshot
Read from a snapshot

client.listConfigurationSettingsForSnapshot("release-1.0")
      .forEach(s -> System.out.println(s.getKey() + " = " + s.getValue()));

for s in client.list_configuration_settings(snapshot_name="release-1.0"):
    print(f"{s.key} = {s.value}")

client.recoverSnapshot("release-1.0");   // status → ready

client.archive_snapshot("release-1.0")
client.recover_snapshot("release-1.0")

docs.text:
Type Behaviour key (default) One entry per key; last matching filter wins when keys overlap key_label One entry per (key, label) pair; no deduplication JavaPython 
new ConfigurationSnapshot(filters)
    .setSnapshotComposition(SnapshotComposition.KEY_LABEL);

from azure.appconfiguration import SnapshotComposition

client.begin_create_snapshot(
    name="all-envs",
    filters=[ConfigurationSettingsFilter(key="app/*")],
    composition_type=SnapshotComposition.KEY_LABEL,

docs.title: REST API Reference
docs.text: All endpoints sit under /{accountName}-appconfig/ with an api-version query parameter (e.g. ?api-version=2023-11-01).

docs.title: Key-Values
docs.text: Method Path Description GET / HEAD /kv List key-values (supports key, label filters) GET / HEAD /kv/{key} Get a key-value PUT /kv/{key} Set a key-value DELETE /kv/{key} Delete a key-value

docs.title: Keys & Labels
docs.text: Method Path Description GET / HEAD /keys List distinct key names GET / HEAD /labels List distinct labels

docs.title: Revisions
docs.text: Method Path Description GET / HEAD /revisions List revision history (supports key, label filters)

docs.title: Locks
docs.text: Method Path Description PUT /locks/{key} Lock a key-value (prevents modification) DELETE /locks/{key} Unlock a key-value

docs.title: Snapshots
docs.text: Method Path Description GET / HEAD /snapshots List snapshots (supports name filter) GET / HEAD /snapshots/{name} Get a snapshot PUT /snapshots/{name} Create a snapshot PATCH /snapshots/{name} Archive or recover a snapshot GET /kv?snapshot={name} List frozen key-values from a snapshot

docs.title: Operations (LRO polling)
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /operations?snapshot={name} Poll snapshot creation status (always returns Succeeded)

docs.title: Conditional Operations (ETags)
docs.text:
Every key-value response includes an ETag header. Use If-Match for optimistic concurrency:

# Conditional update: only succeeds if ETag matches
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-appconfig/kv/my-key" \
  -H "If-Match: \"<etag>\"" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value": "new-value"}'

A mismatch returns 412 Precondition Failed. A locked key returns 423 Locked.

docs.title: Azure Resource Manager (ARM)
docs.text:
The central management-plane handler. It serves the generic ARM surface (subscriptions, resource groups, and the resource/provider listings) that the hashicorp/azurerm Terraform provider, OpenTofu, and the Azure CLI expect, and it acts as the fallthrough for management-plane paths not claimed by a more specific handler (AKS, SQL, Redis, Managed Identity, and the other Microsoft.* providers).

HTTP-only: no Docker. ARM resource state (resource groups and the ARM shells) is in-memory and ephemeral; it does not persist across restarts regardless of storage.mode. The tenant and subscription directory is the exception: it follows storage.mode (see Tenants and subscriptions), and so do resource groups under resource-group-semantics (see Resource groups).

Disabling ARM disables the management plane

arm.enabled: false turns off /subscriptions and /providers routing, which the provider-specific ARM services (Redis, SQL, AKS, …) depend on. Leave it enabled unless you are deliberately testing a data-plane-only configuration.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Tenants and subscriptions: a directory of tenants (each in one cloud) and subscriptions (each owned by one tenant, in one state). GET /tenants and GET /subscriptions (enumeration, used by az login) list it; an unknown subscription id is registered on first use, or refused with 404 SubscriptionNotFound under parity: strict
  • Locations: GET /subscriptions/{sub}/locations, the region catalog of the subscription's cloud, read by az account list-locations, the CLI's display-name location translation (-l "East US"), and Terraform's data.azurerm_location
  • Resource groups: CreateOrUpdate, Get, CheckExistence (HEAD), Update (PATCH), Delete, List (/subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}), scoped per subscription, names matched case-insensitively; tags and managedBy are kept; accepts both resourceGroups and the lowercase resourcegroups spelling. See Resource groups
  • Storage accounts: an ARM shell that bridges Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts to the live Blob and Queue backends, returning the well-known development account key
  • Key vaults and managed HSMs: ARM shells for Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults and managedHSMs whose vaultUri and hsmUri point at the live Key Vault handler, kept in the arm-keyvault store under the global storage mode
  • Sites: an ARM shell for Microsoft.Web/sites and its config/web that provisions a Functions app from linuxFxVersion, kept in the arm-web store under the global storage mode
  • Resource listing: GET /subscriptions/{sub}/resources and POST .../{namespace}/checkNameAvailability
  • Resource providers: every namespace floci-az serves, with its resource types and Azure's api-versions, and register/unregister (see Resource providers)
  • Provider fallthrough: management-plane paths for providers without a dedicated handler are answered here so Terraform reads and dependency lookups resolve

docs.text:

PUT    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}
GET    /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}
HEAD   /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}

POST   /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/{namespace}/unregister

azurerm_storage_account and azurerm_key_vault resolve to those two provider paths; the storage account returns the well-known development key and the vault's vaultUri points at the live Key Vault data plane.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Point Terraform at the emulator with a minimal azurerm provider block (see the Terraform guide for the full setup):

provider "azurerm" {
  features {}
  # metadata_host / endpoints redirected at localhost:4577: see the Terraform guide
}

resource "azurerm_resource_group" "example" {
  name     = "my-rg"
  location = "eastus"
}

Or drive it directly:

curl -s -X PUT \
  "http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/resourceGroups/my-rg?api-version=2021-04-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"location":"eastus"}'

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  parity: compat                     # compat | azure | strict
  # parity-overrides:
  #   subscription-listing: true     # default: on from azure
  #   strict-subscriptions: true     # default: on from strict
  #   resource-group-semantics: true # default: on from azure
  #   resource-group-delete: true    # default: on from azure
  #   strict-resource-groups: true   # default: on from strict
  #   strict-providers: true         # default: on from strict
  #   location-normalize: true       # default: on from azure
  #   tenant-scoping: true           # default: on from azure
  #   strict-locations: true         # default: on from strict
  #   strict-names: true             # default: on from strict
  cloud:
    default: AzureCloud
  services:
    arm:
      enabled: true
      default-subscription-id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
  storage:
    services:
      directory:
        # mode: persistent           # default: storage.mode
Property Env var Default Description services.arm.enabled FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ARM_ENABLED true Enables the ARM management plane. Disabling it turns off every ARM-based service services.arm.default-subscription-id FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ARM_DEFAULT_SUBSCRIPTION_ID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 The subscription that always exists, listed first by GET /subscriptions, so the one az login selects parity FLOCI_AZ_PARITY compat The Azure parity level, compat, azure or strict; see Parity levels parity-overrides.subscription-listing FLOCI_AZ_PARITY_OVERRIDES_SUBSCRIPTION_LISTING on from azure true: GET /subscriptions also lists subscriptions registered on first use, and GET /subscriptions/{sub} echoes the directory's id rather than the path's spelling parity-overrides.strict-subscriptions FLOCI_AZ_PARITY_OVERRIDES_STRICT_SUBSCRIPTIONS on from strict true: an unknown subscription is 404 SubscriptionNotFound. false: it is registered on first use parity-overrides.resource-group-semantics FLOCI_AZ_PARITY_OVERRIDES_RESOURCE_GROUP_SEMANTICS on from azure true: a resource-group re-PUT answers 200, a resource PUT under a missing group creates the group, and groups persist in the directory store parity-overrides.resource-group-delete FLOCI_AZ_PARITY_OVERRIDES_RESOURCE_GROUP_DELETE on from azure true: a resource-group DELETE deletes every resource in the group and answers 202 with a Location to poll; the generic listings also show Event Grid, Monitor and Email resources parity-overrides.strict-resource-groups FLOCI_AZ_PARITY_OVERRIDES_STRICT_RESOURCE_GROUPS on from strict true: a request for a resource under a group that does not exist is 404 ResourceGroupNotFound, and groups are kept in the directory store cloud.default FLOCI_AZ_CLOUD_DEFAULT AzureCloud The cloud of the default tenant and of a tenant that names none: AzureCloud, AzureUSGovernment or AzureChinaCloud. An unknown name fails startup. Today it changes which cloud tenants and request scopes resolve to and the default location of a new group; endpoints, token issuers, DNS suffixes and TLS names stay the public cloud's, and a startup warning says so cloud.<name>.default-location FLOCI_AZ_CLOUD_<NAME>_DEFAULT_LOCATION the cloud's first catalog location The location a resource or group of that cloud gets when its request names none; see Resource locations tenants[n].* FLOCI_AZ_TENANTS_<n>__ID, ..._DISPLAY_NAME, ..._DEFAULT_DOMAIN, ..._CLOUD none Extra tenants; see below subscriptions[n].* FLOCI_AZ_SUBSCRIPTIONS_<n>__ID, ..._TENANT_ID, ..._DISPLAY_NAME, ..._STATE none Extra subscriptions; see below storage.services.directory.mode FLOCI_AZ_STORAGE_SERVICES_DIRECTORY_MODE storage.mode Storage mode of the tenant and subscription directory

The default tenant comes from the Entra ID default-tenant-id setting (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002 by default), so GET /tenants, the subscription's tenantId and issued tokens always agree. The Managed Identity system-assigned-scope defaults to subscriptions/${floci-az.services.arm.default-subscription-id}, so it follows the subscription when you change it.

docs.title: Cloud metadata
docs.text:
GET /metadata/endpoints describes the cloud with every endpoint a client calls at the emulator's own base URL (the request's scheme and host, or the X-Forwarded-Proto scheme behind a TLS proxy), in the shape the api-version asks for:

api-version Shape Read by 2022-09-01, or any other, or none one object, named floci-az azurerm's metadata_host, az cloud register --endpoint-resource-manager 2019-05-01 a list holding one cloud, named floci-az the az CLI's ARM_CLOUD_METADATA_URL 2018-01-01 Azure's cloudEndpoint document azurerm's location validation

The 2019-05-01 and 2018-01-01 answers start from Azure's own payload for the default cloud (floci-az.cloud.default), so audiences and suffixes of services no client reaches through this document stay Azure's. Setting ARM_CLOUD_METADATA_URL to <base-url>/metadata/endpoints?api-version=2019-05-01 is enough for the az CLI: the one cloud listed becomes its active cloud without az cloud register or az cloud set, and az login signs in against the emulator. The cloud is named floci-az rather than AzureCloud because az replaces the login endpoint of a cloud named AzureCloud with Microsoft's. Use the https base URL: MSAL refuses a plain-HTTP authority.

The 2018-01-01 cloudEndpoint lists Azure's ARM hosts verbatim and none of the emulator's. azurerm validates a resource's location only against the entry whose endpoint is its own ARM host, so it keeps accepting any non-empty location against floci-az, as before.

docs.title: Tenants and subscriptions
docs.text:
The directory holds the default tenant and subscription, the ones listed under floci-az.tenants and floci-az.subscriptions, and the subscriptions registered on first use:

floci-az:
  tenants:
    - id: 11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
      display-name: Contoso Gov        # default: floci-az local
      default-domain: contoso.example  # default: floci-az.local
      cloud: AzureUSGovernment         # default: cloud.default
  subscriptions:
    - id: 22222222-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
      tenant-id: 11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000000   # default: the default tenant
      display-name: contoso-dev                         # default: floci-az local
      state: Enabled                                    # Enabled, Warned, PastDue, Disabled or Deleted

Only id is required. An entry with the default tenant's or subscription's id overrides it in place, for example to start the default subscription Disabled. A subscription must name the default tenant or a configured one, and an unknown cloud or state fails startup with the property that holds it.

  • Cloud: a tenant lives in exactly one cloud, and a subscription's cloud is its tenant's. A request under /subscriptions/{sub} resolves to that cloud.
  • Listing: GET /subscriptions lists the caller's tenant's subscriptions. By default the caller's tenant is always the default tenant; under tenant-scoping it is the tid of the request's Bearer token, when the directory holds that tenant (see Tenant scoping). The default subscription comes first, then configured ones in config order, so az login (which selects the first Enabled subscription) keeps selecting the default. Subscriptions registered on first use are listed after them only under subscription-listing. GET /tenants lists every tenant, each reported as the caller's Home tenant.
  • Id echo: subscription ids are case-insensitive. By default GET /subscriptions/{sub} echoes the id as the path spells it; under subscription-listing it echoes the directory's spelling (the configured one, or the one the subscription was first used with).
  • Persistence: configured entries are rewritten from configuration at every start, and an entry no longer configured is dropped. First-use entries survive a restart when storage.services.directory.mode (or storage.mode) persists. POST /_admin/reset drops first-use entries. A first-use subscription whose tenant is no longer in the directory after a restart (the default tenant id changed, or a configured tenant was removed) moves to the default tenant.

docs.title: Tenant scoping
docs.text:
With tenant-scoping (on from parity: azure) the tid claim of a request's Bearer token is read as the caller's tenant. The token is decoded, never verified: the claim only picks which tenant's view the request gets, and verifying tokens is strict auth's job.

  • GET /subscriptions lists that tenant's subscriptions, as Azure lists the subscriptions of the tenant a token was issued for. A tenant the directory does not hold, or a request without a readable token, is the default tenant. A tenant that owns no subscription sees the default subscription, so a client logged in to it (az login --tenant) still finds one to use.
  • A subscription used for the first time is registered under the caller's tenant when the directory holds it.
  • GET /tenants still lists every tenant, each as Home. Azure lists every tenant the identity can reach, and every tenant is reachable in the emulator, so az login without --tenant walks every tenant and, with a token per tenant, finds each one's subscriptions.

Emulator choices, with no Azure source to settle them: the default-subscription fallback, and Home for every tenant (no local source says which category a tenant reached as a guest gets).

docs.title: Parity levels
docs.text:
floci-az.parity decides how closely floci-az follows Azure where Azure differs from what floci-az has always answered. The levels nest, and every parity-overrides key defaults from the level, so one key can also be set alone to opt in piecemeal:

Level What changes compat (default) Nothing a client could rely on: unknown subscriptions are registered internally on first use but not listed, ids are echoed as sent, and resource groups answer as they always have (every PUT 201, DELETE 200 without cascade) azure Azure's answers for the requests Azure accepts. Every parity override on: subscription-listing, resource-group-semantics, resource-group-delete, location-normalize, tenant-scoping strict azure plus Azure's refusals, every strict-* override: strict-subscriptions, strict-resource-groups, strict-providers, strict-locations, strict-names

auth.mode plays no part in any of this. The startup banner prints parity: <level> followed by every override set to a value its level would not give it. At the default level the line also names the variable that changes it, since a misspelt variable is silently ignored.

When an override refuses a request, the response body is Azure's own and says nothing about floci-az; the emulator's log has one INFO line per refusal naming the override that caused it. Under azure, a subscription registered on first use is logged at WARN, because it is now listed where Azure would answer 404.

docs.title: First use and strict subscriptions
docs.text:
Request names a subscription that is Default strict-subscriptions (on from parity: strict) in the directory, Enabled or PastDue served served in the directory, Warned, Disabled or Deleted GET, HEAD and DELETE served; PUT, PATCH and POST refused with 409 ReadOnlyDisabledSubscription same not in the directory registered on first use (Enabled, default tenant), then served; listed only under subscription-listing 404 SubscriptionNotFound: The subscription '{id}' could not be found.

By default any id is accepted, GUID or not, so Terraform and SDK clients configured with their own subscription keep working. Strict subscriptions do not check the format: a malformed id is simply not in the directory, and Azure documents SubscriptionNotFound for a wrong or wrongly formatted id too.

Emulator choices, with no Azure source to settle them:

  • The refusal of a write on a read-only subscription: Azure's resource provider contract says only GET and DELETE work on a warned or suspended subscription, but no local source gives the status and code a client receives. floci-az answers 409 ReadOnlyDisabledSubscription.
  • PastDue is a billing state the provider contract does not list; floci-az keeps it writable.
  • Deleted is read-only like Disabled. Azure cleans a deleted subscription's resources up; floci-az does not cascade them.

docs.title: Resource groups
docs.text:
Resource groups follow the ResourceGroups operations of the Resources REST spec (the az CLI pins 2024-11-01, azurerm 2023-07-01; both declare the same status codes). Names are matched case-insensitively, and a group answers with the spelling of its latest PUT; a PATCH in another casing updates the group and keeps that spelling.

These hold in every configuration:

  • Tags and managedBy: a PUT keeps both and every read returns them; a group created without tags has no tags key.
  • PATCH answers 200 with the group. tags and managedBy replace what they name (a tags object replaces the whole tag set, as azurerm expects when it sends its full tag map); everything the body leaves out is kept. A missing group is 404 ResourceGroupNotFound.
  • HEAD answers 204 for a group and 404 without one.

The rest depends on the parity overrides:

Behaviour Default Override PUT of an existing group 201, as for a new one resource-group-semantics: 200 GET of a missing group 404 ResourceGroupNotFound, Resource group '{rg}' could not be found., as Azure answers the same Resource PUT under a missing group the resource is created, no group appears resource-group-semantics: the group is created once the resource is (only after a 2xx), in the location the resource reports, else the cloud's default location. strict-resource-groups: refused with 404 ResourceGroupNotFound before the resource's handler runs, as is a read, an action or a delete of a resource under a missing group DELETE 200; only the group is removed, a missing group is 200 too resource-group-delete: see below Persistence in memory, lost on restart resource-group-semantics or strict-resource-groups: kept in the directory store, so they follow storage.services.directory.mode Generic listings (.../resources) as before: Event Grid topics, Log Analytics workspaces, data collection endpoints and rules, and Communication and Email services are not listed resource-group-delete: listed, so Terraform's prevent_deletion_if_contains_resources sees what a delete would remove

Under resource-group-delete a DELETE of a group is the long-running operation the spec declares:

  1. Every resource the generic index holds in the group is deleted, the deepest ids first, by sending the resource's own DELETE through the same routing and handler a client request reaches, so each service applies its own side effects (a global name is released, a sidecar container stopped). A resource that is already gone counts as deleted; any other failure is logged and the delete goes on.
  2. The group is removed and the request answers 202 with a Location of {scheme}://{host}/subscriptions/{sub}/operationresults/{id}?api-version=..., built from the request's own scheme and host, and Retry-After: 1.
  3. The work is done by the time the Location is polled: it answers 200 with an empty body, the shape Azure's own poll ends with. A missing group is 404 ResourceGroupNotFound.

While the delete runs, the group is marked as being deleted, so that no resource created meanwhile is left behind: a PUT or PATCH of a resource under the group is refused with 409 ResourceGroupBeingDeleted, and the delete waits for any such request that was already running before it lists the group's resources. The mark is removed when the delete ends, whether it removed the group or failed. Without resource-group-delete nothing is marked and no request is refused.

Emulator choices, with no Azure source to settle them: a re-PUT with a different location replaces the location, as floci-az always has (Azure documents the location as fixed at creation but no local source gives the error it answers); Retry-After is 1 second (Azure sends none on this operation, and clients then fall back to their own, much longer, poll interval); forceDeletionTypes is accepted and ignored; a write under a group that is being deleted answers 409 with the message The resource group '{rg}' is in deprovisioning state and cannot perform this operation. (Azure documents the ResourceGroupBeingDeleted code, with the advice to wait for the deletion to complete, but not its status or message).

docs.title: Template deployments
docs.text: Microsoft.Resources/deployments is served by its own handler; see ARM Template Deployments.

docs.title: Resource providers
docs.text:
GET /subscriptions/{sub}/providers lists every namespace floci-az serves, and only those: a namespace it does not serve is left out, which azurerm reads as nothing to register, and any request naming one is 404 InvalidResourceNamespace. Each namespace carries the resource types floci-az serves in it, with Azure's api-versions newest first, the regions a type can be created in by display name, and registrationPolicy: RegistrationFree for Microsoft.Resources, RegistrationRequired for the rest.

register and unregister answer 200 with the Provider body in its final state, Registered or Unregistered, at once and every time. Azure passes through Registering and Unregistering first, but az provider register --wait and the Python SDK's auto-register policy poll without a limit, so a transitional state would only make them wait.

By default every namespace is Registered, so nothing ever needs registering, as before. With strict-providers (on from parity: strict) every namespace but Microsoft.Resources starts NotRegistered in each subscription, and a request for one of its resource types is refused with Azure's 409 MissingSubscriptionRegistration until the namespace is registered. A DELETE is never refused, so resources created before their namespace was unregistered can still be deleted, by a client or by a resource group delete. The Go, Java and Python SDKs catch that error, register the namespace and retry on their own; azurerm with resource_provider_registrations set registers what it needs at configure time. Registrations then persist in the directory store, alongside the subscriptions they belong to.

Emulator choices, with no Azure source to settle them: the status and message of InvalidResourceNamespace (Azure documents the code for an unknown namespace, but no recording shows the Providers API answering one), and the capabilities string (SupportsTags, SupportsLocation for a type with a location of its own, None otherwise). defaultApiVersion, apiProfiles, zoneMappings and authorizations are optional in Azure's answer and omitted.

docs.title: Resource locations
docs.text:
A resource or resource group whose request names no location gets its cloud's default location: the cloud's first location in the catalog (eastus for AzureCloud, usgovvirginia for AzureUSGovernment, chinanorth for AzureChinaCloud), or the one configured for that cloud:

floci-az:
  cloud:
    AzureCloud:
      default-location: westeurope   # FLOCI_AZ_CLOUD_AZURECLOUD_DEFAULT_LOCATION

The cloud name is matched without regard to case, so the environment variable form works. The value may be a name or a display name (West Europe) and is stored canonical; a location the cloud does not offer, or a cloud the catalog does not hold, fails startup.

By default a resource's location is stored and echoed exactly as the client sent it, so "East US" and eastus are two different values, and names built from it keep the spelling: a container group's FQDN, an AKS cluster's FQDN and its MC_<group>_<cluster>_<location> node resource group.

With location-normalize (on from parity: azure) the request gate rewrites the location of every PUT or PATCH body of a served resource type before its handler runs, for the cloud the subscription belongs to, as Azure stores it:

  • a display name or any casing becomes the canonical name: "East US 2" is stored and echoed as eastus2, and the ACI and AKS names above use it
  • a global type (DNS zones, private DNS zones and their virtual network links, Communication and Email services) is global whatever the client sends, and a PUT that names no location gets global
  • a type whose location defaults to its group's gets the group's location when a PUT names none

With strict-locations (on from parity: strict) a PUT of a regional resource naming a location its subscription's cloud does not offer is refused before its handler runs with Azure's 400 NoRegisteredProviderFound: "No registered resource provider found for location '' and API version '' for type ''. The supported api-versions are '…'. The supported locations are '…'." global is always accepted. A PATCH, a child resource and a global type are never refused.

Both run before policy evaluation, so policy conditions see the canonical location. A location a policy append adds or changes is checked again after policy, the same way: normalized under location-normalize and refused under strict-locations.

Emulator choices, with no Azure source to settle them: which declared types count as global follows each service's declaration; the supported locations in the message are every location of the cloud, where Azure lists the ones the type is offered in.
