docs.title: Resource names across subscriptions
docs.text:
Two subscriptions can use the same resource-group name, and most resources then coexist: each subscription gets its own identity, virtual network, DNS zone, Event Grid topic, AKS cluster, container group, Container Apps environment or email service under the same name.

Resources whose name is a global DNS name behave as in Azure: the first subscription to create the name owns it. A create of the same name from another subscription or resource group is refused, that scope reads the name as 404, and the name is free again once the owner deletes it. The same holds for child calls: a storage account's containers, queues and listKeys answer 404 under any scope but the owner's, and a path that names no resource group never reaches another subscription's resource. Concurrent creates of one name from several subscriptions leave exactly one owner.

Resource Refused with Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts 409 StorageAccountAlreadyTaken, or 409 StorageAccountInAnotherResourceGroup within the same subscription Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults 409 VaultAlreadyExists Microsoft.KeyVault/managedHSMs 409 Conflict (see below) Microsoft.Web/sites 409 in the App Service error shape (Code: Conflict, ExtendedCode: 54001) Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries 409 AlreadyInUse Microsoft.Cache/redis 409 NameNotAvailable Microsoft.Sql/servers 400 NameAlreadyExists Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers, Microsoft.DBforMySQL/flexibleServers, Microsoft.DBforMariaDB/servers 409 ServerNameAlreadyExists Microsoft.ApiManagement/service 409 ServiceAlreadyExists Microsoft.Communication/communicationServices 409 Conflict (see below)

POST /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Storage/checkNameAvailability, the Microsoft.KeyVault equivalent and its checkMhsmNameAvailability, and the Microsoft.Web one for a site name report a taken name as nameAvailable: false, reason AlreadyExists. For Microsoft.Storage, malformed names report nameAvailable: false, reason AccountNameInvalid. Storage account names must contain 3 to 24 lowercase letters or digits. A PUT that creates a storage account with such a name is refused with 400 AccountNameInvalid.

The codes come from Microsoft's troubleshooting pages and real error payloads, because the REST specs do not model create conflicts. No public source gives the code for Managed HSM or Communication Services, so those two answer with ARM's generic Conflict. The status for the PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB servers is not publicly documented either; 409 is the likeliest.

docs.title: Intentional deviations
docs.text:
• Unknown subscriptions exist on first use: unless strict-subscriptions is on, any subscription id a request names is registered and served (and listed under subscription-listing), so a client configured with its own subscription id keeps working. ARM state is kept per subscription.
  • The caller's tenant is the default tenant unless tenant-scoping is on, and even then the token is read for its tid only, never verified.
  • Locations are a static catalog per cloud: a subscription lists the regions of the cloud its tenant belongs to (the public cloud's 51, US Gov's 6 or China's 6), with names and display names from the Azure SDK's region list; every entry is a physical region with zones 1 to 3 mapped to <region>-az<n>. regionalDisplayName repeats displayName, and geography, geographyGroup, latitude, longitude, physicalLocation and pairedRegion are omitted. There are no edge zones, so includeExtendedLocations=true returns the same list. Location values on resources are echoed as sent and not validated unless location-normalize or strict-locations is on (see Resource locations).
  • ARM state is in-memory: resource groups and the ARM shells do not persist across restarts; only the tenant and subscription directory follows storage.mode, and resource groups too under resource-group-semantics.
  • Resource-group deletion does not cascade by default: deleting a group leaves resources created under it behind (they still appear in GET .../resources, so Terraform's prevent_deletion_if_contains_resources works). resource-group-delete turns the cascade on.
  • Shared Key / ARM auth is accepted but not verified: any bearer token or Shared Key is honored, consistent with the rest of the emulator's permissive dev auth.

docs.title: Blob Storage
docs.text:
Compatible with the azure-storage-blob SDKs (Java, Python, Node.js), focused Java azure-storage-file-datalake SDK flows, the Azure CLI (az storage blob), and Azurite-style connection strings. Speaks the Azure Storage Blob REST protocol with Shared Key authentication, Blob XML responses, and the Data Lake Storage Gen2 DFS host alias.

HTTP-only: no Docker. Data is held by the configured storage backend (memory by default; persistent, hybrid, or wal for durability).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Containers: Create, Get properties, Delete, List (?comp=list); duplicate create returns 409 ContainerAlreadyExists
  • Blobs: Put (upload), Get (download), Delete, List within a container; overwrite semantics
  • Block blobs: staged block upload (?comp=block) followed by commit (?comp=blocklist) for large payloads, in addition to single-request Put Blob
  • Data Lake Storage Gen2 endpoint alias: the {account}.dfs.core.windows.net host maps to the Blob backend so ADLS SDK path clients can create, read, write, and delete paths through the same local data store
  • User delegation key vending: POST ?restype=service&comp=userdelegationkey returns Azure-shaped XML for SDK-generated user delegation SAS flows
  • User delegation SAS enforcement: validates SDK-generated user delegation SAS signatures, expiry, signed key validity, permissions, and container/blob/directory resource scope for Blob and ADLS path operations
  • ADLS Gen2 / Hadoop ABFS 3.3.4 path operations - supports the DFS wire shapes used by org.apache.hadoop:hadoop-azure:3.3.4: conditional file/directory create, path status and properties, append/flush, recursive delete, file/directory rename, POSIX owner/group/permission/ACL metadata, checkAccess, and the ADLS Path Lease POST API. Hadoop's default conditional-create overwrite flow (409 -> status/ETag -> If-Match) is modeled explicitly. Access-control operations require an HNS-enabled account. Accounts listed in hierarchical-namespace-accounts have HNS enabled by default; ARM-created accounts can also enable it with properties.isHnsEnabled: true. Other custom account names use a flat namespace by default. As in Azure, HNS is fixed when the account is created: a later PUT that sends a different isHnsEnabled value returns 400 AccountPropertyCannotBeUpdated, while a PUT that omits the property keeps the current setting.
  • ADLS filesystem operations - create/delete a filesystem and get/set filesystem properties via ?resource=filesystem. Root getAccessControl is supported so Hadoop can auto-detect HNS and resolve getFileStatus("/") without forcing fs.azure.account.hns.enabled=true.
  • ADLS Path - List - supports Java DataLake SDK listPaths and Hadoop listStatus, including recursive/non-recursive listing, directory filters, exact-file singleton results, server pagination, and Hadoop 3.3.4's Base64 HNS startFrom continuation token.
  • ADLS AppendBlob mode - recognizes Hadoop's blobType=AppendBlob create mode and enforces sequential append positions, including append requests carrying flush=true / close=true.
  • Range download: Range: bytes=… returns 206 Partial Content
  • Conditional download: If-Match / If-None-Match honored; a stale ETag is rejected
  • ETags: sent in the quoted 0x hex form the Blob service uses ("0x8DC1A2B3C4D5E6F"). List Blobs reports each blob's ETag without the quotes, as Azurite does. A container keeps the ETag and Last-Modified from Create Container, so Get Container Properties and List Containers repeat them
  • Metadata: x-ms-meta-* set on upload and returned on Get, round-tripped exactly
  • Blob index tags: Get and Set Blob Tags (?comp=tags, including on a snapshot), x-ms-tags on Put Blob and Put Block List, and x-ms-tag-count on Get Blob and Get Blob Properties. Tag sets are validated (at most 10 tags, keys of 1 to 128 characters, values of up to 256, letters, digits, space and + - . / : = _). Setting tags leaves the blob's ETag and Last-Modified unchanged
  • Find Blobs by Tags: GET ?comp=blobs&where=... across the account and GET /{container}?restype=container&comp=blobs&where=... within one container, with =, >, >=, <, <=, AND, parentheses and @container, and maxresults/marker paging. Each result lists the blob's values for the tags the expression names. Snapshots are not indexed
  • x-ms-if-tags conditions: honored on Get Blob, Get Blob Properties, Put Blob, Append Block, Delete Blob, Get/Set Blob Metadata, Snapshot Blob and Get/Set Blob Tags (which also take x-ms-blob-if-match and x-ms-blob-if-none-match); the expression also accepts OR and <>
  • Copy Blob and Copy Blob From URL: PUT with x-ms-copy-source (and x-ms-requires-sync: true for Copy Blob From URL) copies a blob, or a snapshot of one with ?snapshot=, from any container or account in the emulator. The source may be a path-style URL, a host-style URL ({account}.blob.{host}) or a bare /{account}/{container}/{blob} path. Metadata is the source's, or the x-ms-meta-* headers when the request sends any; destination conditions and leases are enforced, and an existing destination must be of the source's blob type (409 InvalidBlobType). A new destination needs create permission and an existing one write permission, as for Put Blob. Tags are the request's x-ms-tags, never the source's, except that Copy Blob From URL with x-ms-copy-source-tag-option: COPY keeps the source's. A SAS on the source URL is checked as a read of the source, as Azurite checks it, and a failed check is CannotVerifyCopySource with the status the read got. The x-ms-source-if-match, -if-none-match, -if-modified-since and -if-unmodified-since conditions are checked against the source (412 SourceConditionNotMet). Both answer 202 with x-ms-copy-status: success
  • Put Blob From URL and Put Block From URL: PUT with x-ms-copy-source and x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob writes a block blob holding the source's bytes, and ?comp=block with x-ms-copy-source stages the source, or its x-ms-source-range, as a block. Sources are found, SAS-checked and conditioned as for Copy Blob; a missing source is 404 CannotVerifyCopySource, a range starting past the source's end is 416 CannotVerifyCopySource, a malformed range or a request body is 400 InvalidHeaderValue, and an x-ms-source-content-md5 that does not match is 400 Md5Mismatch. A source written with a customer-provided key is read only with that key in x-ms-source-encryption-key (and its -sha256); a missing or different key is 409 CannotVerifyCopySource. Put Blob From URL keeps Put Blob's destination rules (conditions, leases, If-None-Match: *); its content properties are the source's unless x-ms-copy-source-blob-properties: false, an x-ms-blob-* header sets its own property either way, request metadata replaces the source's, and tags are the request's or, with x-ms-copy-source-tag-option: COPY, the source's (400 when both are sent). Both answer 201 with the copied bytes' Content-MD5
  • ARM containers and queues: .../blobServices/default/containers/{name} and .../queueServices/default/queues/{name} answer from the data plane's own containers and queues, so a container or queue made on either plane is read on the other, and an ARM delete removes it with its blobs or messages. A missing one is 404 (ContainerNotFound / QueueNotFound, the Storage service's codes; Azure's ARM spec records no code for it). Statuses follow the spec: a container delete is 200, or 204 when there was none; a queue create is 200 and a queue delete 204
  • Not-found semantics: missing blob/container returns the Azure 404 BlobNotFound / ContainerNotFound XML error shape

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
http://localhost:4577/{account}/{container}                  # container operations
http://localhost:4577/{account}/{container}/{blob}           # blob operations
http://localhost:4577/{account}/{filesystem}?resource=filesystem&recursive=true  # ADLS listPaths

The account also answers at the host-style address {account}.blob.core.windows.net (and the Data Lake Gen2 alias {account}.dfs.core.windows.net, which maps to the same blob backend) when the Host header is set, matching how the SDKs address storage endpoints.

ARM storage account responses include both blob and dfs primary endpoints so Data Lake SDK clients can discover the Gen2 endpoint shape.

ARM storage accounts are kept in the arm-storage store, which follows the global storage mode, so under persistent or hybrid an account survives a restart with its data, its tags and its isHnsEnabled setting. ARM ids are case-insensitive: a PUT that differs from the account's id only in case updates that account, and responses keep the casing of its first PUT. An account name is owned by one account across every subscription, resource group and cloud until that account is deleted; checkNameAvailability answers from that ownership.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
PythonAzure CLI 
from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient

conn = ("DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;"
        "AccountKey=Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw==;"
        "BlobEndpoint=http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1;")
svc = BlobServiceClient.from_connection_string(conn)
container = svc.create_container("my-container")
container.upload_blob("hello.txt", b"hello world")
print(container.download_blob("hello.txt").readall())

az storage container create --name my-container \
  --connection-string "DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;AccountKey=...;BlobEndpoint=http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1;"

The well-known Azurite development key (Eby8vdM0…) is accepted; any account name works.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    blob:
      enabled: true
      hierarchical-namespace-accounts: devstoreaccount1
  storage:
    services:
      blob:
        # mode: wal            # override the global storage.mode for blob only
        flush-interval-ms: 5000
Property Env var Default Description enabled FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_BLOB_ENABLED true Enables the Blob Storage service hierarchical-namespace-accounts FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_BLOB_HIERARCHICAL_NAMESPACE_ACCOUNTS devstoreaccount1 Comma-separated account names with hierarchical namespace enabled storage.services.blob.mode FLOCI_AZ_STORAGE_SERVICES_BLOB_MODE (inherits storage.mode) Per-service backend override (memory / persistent / hybrid / wal) storage.services.blob.flush-interval-ms FLOCI_AZ_STORAGE_SERVICES_BLOB_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS 5000 Background flush-to-disk interval for the hybrid mode only; ignored by memory / persistent / wal (wal compacts on storage.wal.compaction-interval-ms instead)

docs.title: Intentional deviations
docs.text:
• Shared Key signatures are accepted but not cryptographically verified: the emulator is a local dev target; any well-formed Authorization header (or the Azurite key) is honored.
  • ADLS large-operation behavior is simplified - directory rename and recursive delete complete atomically in the local backend rather than reproducing Azure's server-side multi-request batching. Hadoop observes a completed operation with no continuation token, which is protocol-compatible for the caller. The full Azure source/destination lease-transfer and time-condition matrix is not modeled.
  • ADLS access control is metadata-compatible, not a full POSIX authorization engine - owner, group, permissions and ACLs round-trip through the Hadoop/DFS wire protocol, and checkAccess validates path existence and request shape. It does not deny requests based on emulated POSIX ACLs; authentication/SAS authorization remains the emulator's access-control boundary.
  • ADLS close/event semantics are storage-only - close=true is accepted and committed data is immediately visible, but Azure Event Grid/change-notification side effects are not emulated.
  • SAS enforcement supports shared-key service SAS and user delegation SAS. Service SAS signatures use floci-az.auth.storage-account-keys, a map from account names to base64 keys. Accounts without an explicit entry use the standard Azurite key, including ARM-created accounts. Explicit entries take precedence. ARM listKeys on a storage account returns the same key (configured or default) as key1 and key2, so a SAS signed with a listed key is accepted. Invalid signatures are rejected, including in dev mode, as are expired tokens and operations outside the granted permissions. This is separate from the permissive Shared Key Authorization header behavior above. Shared-key service SAS supports directory scope (sr=d). Directory service SAS requires sdd and version 2020-02-10 or later. SDK-generated user delegation SAS tokens for container (sr=c), blob (sr=b), Blob snapshot (sr=bs), and ADLS directory (sr=d) resources are validated. Account SAS, stored access policies, IP/protocol restrictions, and the full SAS feature matrix are not fully modeled. User delegation keys are protected by a process-local secret, so SAS tokens issued by a previous emulator process are invalid after restart.
  • Copies complete at once and stay inside the emulator. Copy Blob reports success in its 202, so there is no pending state to poll and Abort Copy Blob is not served. A source outside the emulator, x-ms-source-if-tags, x-ms-copy-source-authorization, x-ms-content-crc64, and Get Blob Properties' x-ms-copy-* fields are not modeled. A source without a SAS is read like any other request, since the emulator enforces only SAS tokens. Append Block From URL (?comp=appendblock with x-ms-copy-source) answers 501, as does a copy source with any x-ms-blob-type other than BlockBlob.
  • Blob snapshots are modeled. They capture immutable blob state and support creation, reads, and deletion. Listing snapshots with include=snapshots on List Blobs is not modeled. Deleting a base blob with snapshots requires x-ms-delete-snapshots: include or only; mutations other than deletion directed at a snapshot return SnapshotsPresent. Blob versioning and tiering are not modeled.
  • Blob leases and ADLS Path leases share the emulator's in-memory lease state and support acquire/renew/change/release/break. Lease state is intentionally process-local and is lost when the emulator restarts.
  • x-ms-server-encrypted: true is reported although no encryption is performed: blob data is stored as-is by the configured storage backend. The header mirrors the x-ms-request-server-encrypted already returned on upload and exists for SDK compatibility.

docs.title: Azure Container Apps
docs.text:
Compatible with Azure Resource Manager clients using Microsoft.App/managedEnvironments and Microsoft.App/containerApps.

Real mode runs each active revision replica as Docker containers. Mocked mode keeps full ARM and revision state without starting Docker.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Managed Environment create, get, update, delete, and list
  • Container App create, get, update, delete, and list
  • Versioned templates with Single and Multiple active revision modes
  • Revision list, get, activate, deactivate, and restart
  • Container commands, arguments, environment variables, and secret references
  • External and internal HTTP ingress forwarded to running revision containers
  • Weighted revision traffic and round-robin replica selection with unhealthy replica failover
  • minReplicas and maxReplicas validation; local replicas start at minReplicas
  • Scale-to-zero apps start one replica on first ingress request when maxReplicas permits
  • Mocked mode for Docker-free tests

Scale rules beyond minimum/maximum replicas are retained in ARM responses but are not evaluated locally. Internal ingress accepts only transport peers whose source IP belongs to a Docker IPAM subnet used by a running Container App replica. Forwarded headers cannot make a public caller internal.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Create an environment:

curl -X PUT 'http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/dev/resourceGroups/apps/providers/Microsoft.App/managedEnvironments/local?api-version=2025-07-01' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"location":"eastus","properties":{}}'

Create an externally accessible app:

curl -X PUT 'http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/dev/resourceGroups/apps/providers/Microsoft.App/containerApps/hello?api-version=2025-07-01' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "location":"eastus",
    "properties":{
      "environmentId":"/subscriptions/dev/resourceGroups/apps/providers/Microsoft.App/managedEnvironments/local",
      "configuration":{
        "activeRevisionsMode":"Single",
        "secrets":[{"name":"token","value":"local-secret"}],
        "ingress":{"external":true,"targetPort":80}
      },
      "template":{
        "revisionSuffix":"v1",
        "containers":[{
          "name":"web",
          "image":"nginx:alpine",
          "env":[{"name":"TOKEN","secretRef":"token"}]
        }],
        "scale":{"minReplicas":1,"maxReplicas":3}
      }
    }
  }'

The response returns a globally unique value in properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn. Route that hostname to floci-az, then call it through port 4577:

FQDN=$(curl -s 'http://localhost:4577/subscriptions/dev/resourceGroups/apps/providers/Microsoft.App/containerApps/hello?api-version=2025-07-01' | jq -r '.properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn')
curl -H "Host: $FQDN" http://localhost:4577/

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    container-apps:
      enabled: true
      mocked: true
      dns-suffix: azurecontainerapps.io
      ingress-timeout-seconds: 60
Environment variable Default Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_CONTAINER_APPS_ENABLED true Enables Microsoft.App routing FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_CONTAINER_APPS_MOCKED true Keeps ARM state without Docker containers FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_CONTAINER_APPS_DNS_SUFFIX azurecontainerapps.io Suffix returned in environment and app FQDNs FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_CONTAINER_APPS_INGRESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60 Backend connect/request timeout

Set mocked: false to enable real mode, which requires access to the Docker daemon. Template containers in one replica share the leader container's network namespace, so sidecars can communicate over localhost. The leader receives the dynamic host-port binding for the shared ingress target port. A replica becomes healthy only after that port accepts TCP connections. Requests still enter floci-az on port 4577.

docs.title: Azure Cosmos DB (SQL API)
docs.text: Compatible with the azure-cosmos SDK (Java, Python, JavaScript, .NET).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Databases: create, get, list, delete (cascade-deletes all containers and documents)
  • Containers: create, replace, get, list, delete; configurable partition key path; custom indexing policies with composite indexes (persisted on create/replace and returned on read)
  • Documents: create, get, replace, delete, list; upsert via x-ms-documentdb-is-upsert header
  • Stored procedures, triggers and user-defined functions: create, get, replace, delete, list and query, stored per container (deleting the container or database removes them). They are stored, never run: see Server-side scripts
  • Time to live (TTL): container defaultTtl (set on create or replace) with per-document ttl overrides; expired documents disappear from reads, lists, queries, and batches
  • Queries: in-process SQL engine with full Cosmos DB SQL dialect support:
  • SELECT *, SELECT c.field1, c.field2, SELECT VALUE c.field, SELECT TOP n
  • WHERE with =, !=, <>, >, >=, <, <=, IN, BETWEEN, NOT, AND, OR, and correlated EXISTS over arrays
  • Logical precedence follows Cosmos DB: NOT binds before AND, then OR; parentheses override that order
  • WHERE functions: IS_DEFINED, IS_NULL, IS_STRING, IS_NUMBER, IS_BOOL, IS_ARRAY, IS_OBJECT, CONTAINS, STARTSWITH, ENDSWITH, ARRAY_CONTAINS
  • ORDER BY field [ASC|DESC], multiple fields: like Azure, an ORDER BY over two or more properties requires a matching composite index on the container, otherwise the query fails with 400 BadRequest (error SC2104)
  • OFFSET n LIMIT m pagination
  • SELECT VALUE COUNT(1) aggregation
  • Named parameters (@param), including array values in ARRAY_CONTAINS(@values, c.field); both membership arguments may be expressions, and NOT ARRAY_CONTAINS(...) excludes matches
  • System properties: _rid, _self, _etag, _ts, _attachments auto-generated on every write
  • Partition keys: resolved from x-ms-documentdb-partitionkey header or extracted from document body using the container's configured path

Queries with x-ms-documentdb-partitionkey (including .NET QueryRequestOptions.PartitionKey) are scoped to the configured logical partition before SQL filtering, aggregation, ordering and pagination. Key values retain their JSON types; [null] and [{}] select null and undefined keys respectively. Omitting the header permits cross-partition queries. Malformed scopes return 400. Writes reject partition headers that disagree with the document body, and patches cannot change partition-key values. Transactional batches enforce the same rules before committing staged writes.

Query continuation tokens bookmark the last source document and its ORDER BY values, including a stable identity to distinguish equal sort values. Deleting an already consumed page, including through transactional batches, does not skip remaining documents. This also applies to projections that omit the sort fields or return scalar values. TOP and OFFSET ... LIMIT retain their total query limits across pages. Tokens are stateless; no server-side query session is required. New tokens are bound to their query text, parameters, account, container identity, and partition scope. Reusing them with a different query or scope returns 400 BadRequest. Parameter order, JSON object member order, and equivalent numeric representations do not change the scope. Array element order remains significant.

Pagination does not provide snapshot isolation for concurrent inserts or changes to sort values. Aggregate, GROUP BY, and DISTINCT queries retain the emulator's existing result-offset pagination; the document bookmark guarantee applies to queries without aggregation or deduplication. Tokens issued by older emulator versions also retain their original offset pagination until completion. Start a new query to use document bookmarks after upgrading.

docs.title: .NET query planner configuration
docs.text:
The account response advertises query-engine capabilities. Floci-AZ emits 20 keys, while the observed Azure gateway payloads contain 19. Two details intentionally differ:

  • sqlAllowLike is true so the advertised capability set matches what Floci-AZ's query engine can execute. Azure currently advertises false.
  • sqlDisableOptimizationFlags does not appear in the observed Azure payloads. Floci-AZ emits the extra key with value 0 so its advertised set remains a superset; no current code reads it.

These are client-planning compatibility values, not user configuration.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
http://localhost:4577/{accountName}-cosmos

Default account: devstoreaccount1 Default endpoint: http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos

docs.title: SDK Connection
Databases
docs.text: Method Path Description POST /dbs Create a database GET /dbs List all databases GET /dbs/{dbId} Get a database DELETE /dbs/{dbId} Delete a database (cascades to containers and documents)

docs.title: Containers (Collections)
docs.text: Method Path Description POST /dbs/{dbId}/colls Create a container GET /dbs/{dbId}/colls List containers GET /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId} Get a container PUT /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId} Replace container properties (e.g. the indexing policy or defaultTtl; id and partition key are immutable) DELETE /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId} Delete a container (cascades to documents)

docs.title: Indexing policies
docs.text:
A custom indexingPolicy (included/excluded paths, composite indexes) supplied on container create or replace is normalized the way Azure does: missing fields are filled with defaults and composite-index path order defaults to ascending: then persisted and returned on container read. The id and partitionKey of a container are immutable on replace, matching Azure.

Composite indexes are enforced for queries: an ORDER BY over two or more properties is only served when the container has a composite index whose paths match the ORDER BY clause exactly (same properties, same sequence, same length) with sort directions matching either exactly or exactly inverted on all paths. Queries without such an index fail with 400 BadRequest ("The order by query does not have a corresponding composite index that it can be served from"), so code that would break in production fails locally too.

{
  "id": "messages",
  "partitionKey": { "paths": ["/conversationId"], "kind": "Hash" },
  "indexingPolicy": {
    "indexingMode": "consistent",
    "automatic": true,
    "includedPaths": [{ "path": "/*" }],
    "excludedPaths": [{ "path": "/\"_etag\"/?" }],
    "compositeIndexes": [[
      { "path": "/conversationId", "order": "ascending" },
      { "path": "/sequence", "order": "ascending" }
    ]]
  }
}

docs.title: Documents
docs.text: Method Path Description POST /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/docs Create a document GET /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/docs List all documents GET /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/docs/{docId} Get a document PUT /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/docs/{docId} Replace a document DELETE /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/docs/{docId} Delete a document

docs.title: Queries
docs.text: POST /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/docs with header x-ms-documentdb-isquery: True (or Content-Type: application/query+json).

docs.title: Server-side scripts
docs.text:
Method Path Description POST /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/{sprocs,triggers,udfs} Create a script (409 Conflict if the id exists) GET /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/{sprocs,triggers,udfs} List scripts (StoredProcedures, Triggers, UserDefinedFunctions) POST same path, with x-ms-documentdb-isquery: True Query scripts with SQL, for example SELECT * FROM root r WHERE r.id = @id GET /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/{sprocs,triggers,udfs}/{id} Get a script PUT /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/{sprocs,triggers,udfs}/{id} Replace a script (honours If-Match) DELETE /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/{sprocs,triggers,udfs}/{id} Delete a script POST /dbs/{dbId}/colls/{collId}/sprocs/{id} Execute a stored procedure: not supported, see below

Every script needs an id and a string body; a trigger also needs triggerType (Pre or Post) and triggerOperation (All, Create, Update, Delete or Replace), matched case-insensitively and returned as sent. A missing or invalid field is 400 BadRequest, on create and on replace, where the id must also match the one in the URL. List and query honour x-ms-max-item-count and x-ms-continuation. Responses carry _rid, _self, _etag and _ts like any other Cosmos resource, so SDK code that registers scripts through container.getScripts() (Java), container.scripts (Python) or container.scripts (JavaScript) works unchanged.

Emulator limitation: scripts are never run. floci-az has no JavaScript runtime:

  • Executing a stored procedure that exists fails with 501 and the Cosmos error body {"code":"NotImplemented","message":"Executing stored procedure '<id>' is not supported: ..."}, which every SDK raises as its Cosmos exception (CosmosException in Java, CosmosHttpResponseError in Python). Executing one that does not exist is 404 NotFound.
  • Pre- and post-triggers named on a document request (x-ms-documentdb-pre-trigger-include, x-ms-documentdb-post-trigger-include) are ignored: the write goes ahead without them.
  • User-defined functions cannot be called from a query (udf.name(...)).

Any other request the emulator does not implement also answers 501 with a {"code":"NotImplemented","message":"..."} body, never an empty response.

docs.title: Create database
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos/dbs \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id": "mydb"}'

docs.title: Create container
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos/dbs/mydb/colls \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id": "items", "partitionKey": {"paths": ["/category"], "kind": "Hash"}}'

docs.title: Create document
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos/dbs/mydb/colls/items/docs \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-ms-documentdb-partitionkey: [\"electronics\"]" \
  -d '{"id": "laptop-1", "category": "electronics", "name": "Laptop Pro", "price": 1299}'

docs.title: Query documents
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos/dbs/mydb/colls/items/docs \
  -H "Content-Type: application/query+json" \
  -H "x-ms-documentdb-isquery: True" \
  -H "x-ms-documentdb-query-enablecrosspartition: True" \
  -d '{
    "query": "SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.price > @minPrice ORDER BY c.price DESC",
    "parameters": [{"name": "@minPrice", "value": 500}]
  }'

docs.title: Query with COUNT
docs.text:
curl -X POST .../docs \
  -H "x-ms-documentdb-isquery: True" \
  -d '{"query": "SELECT VALUE COUNT(1) FROM c WHERE c.category = '\''electronics'\''"}'

Response: {"_rid": "...", "_count": 1, "Documents": [2]}

docs.title: Supported SQL functions
docs.text: Full Azure Cosmos DB SQL grammar implemented in-process.

docs.title: Predicates & type checks
docs.text: Function Description IS_DEFINED(c.field) True if the field exists on the document IS_NULL(c.field) True if the field is null or missing IS_STRING(c.field) True if the value is a string IS_NUMBER(c.field) True if the value is a number IS_INTEGER(c.field) True if the value is an integer IS_BOOL(c.field) True if the value is a boolean IS_ARRAY(c.field) True if the value is an array IS_OBJECT(c.field) True if the value is an object IS_PRIMITIVE(c.field) True if the value is a scalar (string, number, bool, or null) CONTAINS(c.field, 'str' [, true]) String contains; optional 3rd arg for case-insensitive STARTSWITH(c.field, 'prefix' [, true]) String starts-with; optional 3rd arg for case-insensitive ENDSWITH(c.field, 'suffix' [, true]) String ends-with; optional 3rd arg for case-insensitive STRINGEQUALS(c.field, 'val' [, true]) Case-insensitive equality when 3rd arg is true REGEXMATCH(c.field, 'pattern' [, 'flags']) Regular-expression match ARRAY_CONTAINS(c.arr, value) Array contains value LIKE Pattern matching (% wildcard, _ single char)

docs.title: String functions
docs.text: Function Description LOWER(c.field) Convert to lower case UPPER(c.field) Convert to upper case LENGTH(c.field) String length CONCAT(s1, s2, ...) Concatenate strings SUBSTRING(s, start, length) Extract substring TRIM(s) Remove leading and trailing spaces LTRIM(s) / RTRIM(s) Remove leading / trailing spaces REPLACE(s, old, new) Replace occurrences REVERSE(s) Reverse string INDEX_OF(s, sub) Position of first occurrence (−1 if not found) LEFT(s, n) / RIGHT(s, n) Extract leftmost / rightmost n characters TOSTRING(val) Convert value to string STRINGJOIN(separator, arr) Join array elements with separator STRINGSPLIT(s, delimiter) Split string into array

docs.title: Math functions
docs.text: Function Description ABS(n) Absolute value CEILING(n) Smallest integer ≥ n FLOOR(n) Largest integer ≤ n ROUND(n) Round to nearest integer SQRT(n) Square root POWER(base, exp) Exponentiation LOG(n [, base]) Natural log or log base LOG10(n) Base-10 logarithm EXP(n) e^n SIGN(n) −1, 0, or 1 TRUNC(n) Truncate toward zero PI() π RAND() Random number in [0, 1)

docs.title: Array functions
docs.text: Function Description ARRAY_LENGTH(arr) Number of elements ARRAY_SLICE(arr, start [, count]) Extract slice ARRAY_CONCAT(arr1, arr2, ...) Concatenate arrays

docs.title: Conditional
docs.text: Function Description IIF(condition, trueVal, falseVal) Inline if-else expression

docs.title: Upsert
docs.text:
Set x-ms-documentdb-is-upsert: True on POST /docs to create or silently overwrite:

curl -X POST .../docs \
  -H "x-ms-documentdb-is-upsert: True" \
  -d '{"id": "laptop-1", "category": "electronics", "price": 999}'

docs.title: Time to live (TTL)
docs.text:
Containers accept Azure's defaultTtl property on create and replace (-1, or a positive number of seconds up to 2147483647; 0 is rejected with 400, matching Azure). Documents may override it with their own ttl property. Expiry follows the Azure TTL semantics, measured from the document's last modification (_ts):

Container defaultTtl Document ttl Result absent anything TTL disabled: nothing expires -1 absent or -1 never expires -1 m expires m seconds after _ts n absent expires n seconds after _ts n -1 never expires n m expires m seconds after _ts 
# Create a container whose documents expire after one hour
curl -X POST http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos/dbs/mydb/colls \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id": "audit", "partitionKey": {"paths": ["/tenant"], "kind": "Hash"}, "defaultTtl": 3600}'

# Switch TTL off again (omit defaultTtl on replace)
curl -X PUT http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos/dbs/mydb/colls/audit \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id": "audit"}'

Expired documents vanish from point reads, lists, queries, and transactional batches immediately (and no longer block re-creating the same id). Physical deletion is lazy: an expired document is purged when a read next encounters it: mirroring Azure's contract that expired items leave query results at once while background deletion timing is unspecified.

docs.title: Storage Mode
docs.text:
# docker-compose.yml
environment:
  FLOCI_AZ_STORAGE_MODE: memory
  FLOCI_AZ_STORAGE_SERVICES_COSMOS_MODE: wal    # full durability for Cosmos documents

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENABLED true Enable or disable Cosmos DB FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_MOCKED false Master switch: when true, no engine containers are started for any API (equivalent to engines.startup=disabled). The in-process NoSQL/Table paths are unaffected.

docs.title: Multi-API engines
docs.text:
The API reference above covers the always-on SQL / NoSQL endpoint ({account}-cosmos and {account}-cosmos-nosql). Floci AZ also emulates the other Cosmos DB APIs through API-specific engines.

All engines are disabled by default: enable only the APIs your application uses. Four APIs are Docker-backed (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Cassandra, Gremlin): they launch a sidecar container on first request. Two APIs are embedded (NoSQL and Table): in-process, no Docker pull, instant startup.

docs.title: Docker-backed engines
docs.text:
Variable Default Engine image Native port FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_MONGODB_ENABLED false mongo:7 27017 FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_POSTGRESQL_ENABLED false citusdata/citus 5432 FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_CASSANDRA_ENABLED false scylladb/scylla:6.2 9042 FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_GREMLIN_ENABLED false tinkerpop/gremlin-server 8182

You can override the Docker image or host port for any Docker-backed engine:

Variable Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_MONGODB_IMAGE Override the MongoDB image FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_MONGODB_PORT Override the MongoDB host port FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_STARTUP on-demand (default) or eager

docker-compose.yml example (enable MongoDB and PostgreSQL):

services:
  floci-az:
    image: floci/floci-az:latest
    ports:
      - "4577:4577"
      - "27017:27017"   # MongoDB (Cosmos MongoDB API)
      - "5432:5432"     # PostgreSQL (Cosmos PostgreSQL API)
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    environment:
      FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_MONGODB_ENABLED: "true"
      FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_POSTGRESQL_ENABLED: "true"

How it works: when you first send a request to /{account}-cosmos-mongo/, floci-az pulls mongo:7 and starts the container. Subsequent requests go directly to the container's native port (localhost:27017). The /connect endpoint returns the connection string:

curl http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos-mongo/connect
# → {"api":"MONGODB","host":"localhost","port":27017,"connectionString":"mongodb://localhost:27017/","status":"running"}

Do not publish engine ports (27017, 5432, etc.) on the floci-az service. Engines are launched as sibling containers by the host Docker daemon, so they bind ports directly on the host.

With FLOCI_AZ_DOCKER_ENDPOINT_MODE=published (a remote Docker daemon), host and the connection string name the Docker daemon's host and the engine's published port instead of localhost.

docs.title: Embedded engines: NoSQL and Table API (no Docker)
docs.text:
Both engines run entirely inside floci-az: no Docker pull, no container boot time. Data lives in memory; restarting floci-az clears it.

Variable Default Backend FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_NOSQL_ENABLED false In-process SQL engine: full Cosmos DB SQL dialect FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_TABLE_ENABLED false In-memory OData engine (ConcurrentHashMap)

NoSQL engine: activating this endpoint enables the same embedded SQL engine already powering /{account}-cosmos. The /connect endpoint returns https://localhost:4577 as the connection URL (Java SDK requires TLS; enable FLOCI_AZ_TLS_ENABLED=true and fetch the runtime cert from GET /_floci/tls-cert).

Table engine: supported operations: create/delete table · insert/get/replace/merge/delete entity · OData $filter · $top · $select. OData operators: eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, and, or, not.

# Enable the Table engine
export FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_COSMOS_ENGINES_TABLE_ENABLED=true

# Trigger engine activation and retrieve connection string
curl http://localhost:4577/devstoreaccount1-cosmos-table/connect
# → {"api":"TABLE","status":"running","connectionString":"DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;...","notes":"..."}

Use the host and port from the /connect response to build the endpoint, then connect with AzureNamedKeyCredential: the official Cosmos DB for Table pattern (quickstart):

JavaPython 
// official Cosmos DB for Table SDK pattern
String endpoint = "http://" + host + ":" + port + "/devstoreaccount1-cosmos-table";

TableServiceClient client = new TableServiceClientBuilder()
    .endpoint(endpoint)
    .credential(new AzureNamedKeyCredential(
        "devstoreaccount1",
        "Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw=="))
    .buildClient();

from azure.data.tables import TableServiceClient
from azure.core.credentials import AzureNamedKeyCredential

credential = AzureNamedKeyCredential("devstoreaccount1",
    "Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw==")
client = TableServiceClient(
    endpoint=f"http://{host}:{port}/devstoreaccount1-cosmos-table",
    credential=credential)

The connectionString field in the /connect response is also available for SDK clients that prefer the Azure Storage connection string format.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• Stored procedures, triggers, and UDFs are stored but not executed (see Server-side scripts).
  • JOIN with nested arrays is not supported.
  • Change feed is not emulated.
  • Full-text search, vector search, and geospatial queries are not supported.
  • RU/s throughput governance and multi-region replication are out of scope.
  • Partition key paths must be a single top-level field (e.g. /category), not nested paths.

docs.title: ARM Template Deployments
docs.text:
floci-az runs ARM template deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments) at resource-group and subscription scope: the calls behind az deployment group create and az deployment sub create, Terraform's azurerm_resource_group_template_deployment, and any Bicep file once the client has compiled it to ARM JSON.

Each resource in the template is created through the same ARM routing, request gate and handler a client request would reach, so a deployed storage account, virtual network or key vault is exactly the resource a direct PUT creates, and every other floci-az service sees it.

Protocol: ARM REST, JSON

Path: /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{name}, or /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{name} at subscription scope

Api-versions: the Resources spec 2025-04-01, which the az CLI sends; azurerm sends 2020-06-01, whose operations and shapes are the same.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    deployments:
      enabled: true    # FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_DEPLOYMENTS_ENABLED

With enabled: false a deployment path answers the generic ARM 404 ResourceNotFound it answered before deployments existed.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
PUT    .../deployments/{name}                    # CreateOrUpdate: 201 (200 on a re-PUT), Accepted, then runs
GET    .../deployments/{name}/operationStatuses/{id}   # the poll the PUT's Azure-AsyncOperation names
GET    .../deployments/{name}                    # Get
HEAD   .../deployments/{name}                    # CheckExistence: 204 or 404
DELETE .../deployments/{name}                    # Delete: removes the record, never the resources; 204
GET    .../deployments[?$filter=provisioningState eq 'X'&$top=N]   # nextLink when $top leaves more
GET    .../deployments/{name}/operations[/{operationId}]           # also without providers/Microsoft.Resources
POST   .../deployments/{name}/validate           # 200, or 400 with the template error
POST   .../deployments/{name}/exportTemplate     # {"template": ...}
POST   .../deployments/{name}/cancel             # 204 while it runs
POST   .../deployments/{name}/whatIf             # the changes it would make, 200
POST   /providers/Microsoft.Resources/calculateTemplateHash   # {"minifiedTemplate", "templateHash"}

The resource group must exist, or the answer is 404 ResourceGroupNotFound. Every endpoint is served at subscription scope too, under /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments, and at tenant scope, under /providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments.

docs.title: Subscription-scope deployments
docs.text: A subscription-scope deployment deploys subscription-level resources, typically resource groups (Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups, whose id is /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{name}), and policy. As Azure requires, the body carries a location where the deployment's data is stored: a missing one is 400 LocationRequired, and reusing a deployment name with another location is 400 InvalidDeploymentLocation. A resource type that lives in a resource group (a storage account, say) is InvalidTemplate at this scope, and resourceGroup() is an error here. Deploying into a resource group from a subscription-scope template takes a nested deployment (see below), which is what azd provision and a Bicep file with targetScope = 'subscription' and modules send.

docs.title: Tenant-scope deployments
docs.text:
A tenant-scope deployment (az deployment tenant create) carries a location on the same terms as a subscription-scope one, and its tenant is the caller's (the tenant of the request's token when the emulator holds it, otherwise the default tenant). Its own resources are tenant-level ones; a resource that lives in a subscription or a resource group is InvalidTemplate here, and subscription() and resourceGroup() are errors. It reaches a subscription through a nested deployment that names subscriptionId (and location), and a resource group through one that names both subscriptionId and resourceGroup, as Azure requires at this scope. A nested deployment that targets a management group through scope is refused with InvalidTemplate.

resourceId() without a subscription or a resource group takes the deployment's level, as Azure documents: a resource-group id in a resource-group deployment, /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/... at subscription scope, and /providers/... at tenant scope.

docs.title: Nested deployments
docs.text:
A Microsoft.Resources/deployments resource inside a template, which a Bicep module compiles to, is deployed as a deployment of its own at its target: the resource group its resourceGroup property names (in the subscription subscriptionId names, else the parent's), the subscription subscriptionId alone names, or else the parent's own scope. It runs like any other deployment, so it is listed, polled and read at its target, and the parent waits for it: reference('module').outputs.name.value reads its outputs once it has finished.

  • With expressionEvaluationOptions.scope set to inner, as Bicep modules are, the nested template is its own template: its expressions use its own parameters, which the nested deployment's parameters pass in.
  • With outer, the default, its expressions use the parent's parameters and variables: floci-az sends it with the parent's parameters declared as its own (defaulting to the parent's values) and the parent's variable values as its variables. A securestring or secureObject parameter is passed as a parameter value instead of a default, so the child's exportTemplate never shows it. A reference() or list*() call there that names a parent resource is sent naming it by id, since the child does not declare it; an inner-scope deployment nested inside it keeps its own template, whose names are its own. resourceGroup() and subscription() there answer for the nested deployment's own target, where Azure answers the parent's; they differ only when an outer-scope nested deployment targets another scope.

A nested deployment's template is inline or linked (see Linked templates).

docs.title: Linked templates
docs.text:
A deployment's templateLink.uri and parametersLink.uri are downloaded over HTTP or HTTPS when the request arrives, and the deployment runs the downloaded template as if it had been sent inline; the links are echoed in the deployment's properties and in deployment().properties.templateLink. A template staged in floci-az's own blob storage works, the local counterpart of a storage account with a SAS token.

  • A nested deployment's templateLink.relativePath resolves against the link its parent's template came from, keeping the parent link's query string, as Azure does; a parent sent inline has no base, so it is refused. It must stay relative: an absolute URI, or a path such as //other.host/child.json that leaves the parent's scheme, host or port, is 400 InvalidTemplate, so the parent's SAS token never reaches another host.
  • A link that cannot be downloaded (no uri, not HTTP or HTTPS, a non-200 answer, a timeout after 30 seconds, more than 4 MB), whose content is not a JSON object, or whose content carries a different contentVersion than the link names is 400 InvalidContentLink.
  • parameters and parametersLink together are 400 InvalidTemplate, as Azure documents; a parameters link may point at a parameter file ({"parameters": {...}}) or at the parameters object itself.
  • A template spec (templateLink.id) is 400 InvalidTemplate: floci-az does not serve template specs.

docs.title: How a deployment runs
docs.text:
A PUT checks the template at once and answers 201 with provisioningState: Accepted and an Azure-AsyncOperation header, as Azure does. The deployment then runs in the background: the operationStatuses URL answers {"status": "Accepted"} until it ends, then Succeeded, Failed with the error, or Canceled, and GET of the deployment shows Running and then the final state. A PUT or DELETE of a deployment that is still running is 409 DeploymentActive. cancel stops it before its next resource and leaves what it already created in place.

  1. The template is read and checked: parameters (type and allowedValues), variables, resources and outputs. A template floci-az cannot run is refused with 400 InvalidTemplate before anything is created.
  2. Each resource's type, name and dependsOn are evaluated, and the resources are ordered by their dependencies: an explicit dependsOn entry (a name, type/name, or an id), and an implicit dependency for every reference() or list*() call that names a resource by name. As in Azure, resourceId() alone creates no dependency, and a child resource does not depend on its parent unless dependsOn says so. A cycle, or a dependency on a resource the template does not declare, is an InvalidTemplate.
  3. Each resource is evaluated and sent as PUT {id}?api-version={its apiVersion}, without the template-only keys (type, apiVersion, name, dependsOn, condition, comments). A resource whose condition is false is skipped. A 202, or a provisioningState that is not terminal, is polled with GET.
  4. The outputs are evaluated once every resource exists, so reference() reads the live resource.

An extension resource's scope names the resource it extends, as a full id or as the Namespace/type/name of a resource at the deployment's scope (Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/sa1); the resource is created at {scope}/providers/{type}/{name}, a policy assignment or a lock on that one account, say.

Each resource the run tries is a deployment operation (provisioningOperation: Create, with the provider's answer as statusCode, OK or Created, its targetResource, and a statusMessage holding the error when it failed), followed by one EvaluateDeploymentOutput operation, as Azure records them. The operations list is served both under .../providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/{name}/operations and under the spec's own .../resourcegroups/{rg}/deployments/{name}/operations, which has no provider segment and is the form the az CLI sends.

The deployment answers with Azure's DeploymentExtended body: provisioningState, the echoed parameters (a securestring or secureObject value is never echoed), outputs, outputResources, providers, dependencies, templateHash, timestamp, duration and correlationId. When a resource fails, the deployment ends Failed with Azure's DeploymentFailed error, whose details hold the failing resource's own error; a resource that ends in a Failed provisioning state is a ResourceDeploymentFailure.

docs.title: What-if
docs.text: whatIf prepares the deployment as a PUT would, then reads each resource's current state instead of writing it: a resource that does not exist is a Create; one that does is a Modify, with a delta listing each property the template sets to a different value, or a NoChange. Only the properties the template sets are compared, so a provider's own read-only properties never count as changes; after is the current resource with the template's values applied. A nested deployment, and a resource whose expressions cannot be evaluated before deployment (a reference() to a resource the deployment would create), are Unsupported with the reason. whatIfSettings.resultFormat ResourceIdOnly leaves the documents out. The prediction is only as good as the providers' reads: a provider that answers 200 for anything it is asked about makes a new resource look like a NoChange.

docs.title: Child resources
docs.text: A child resource can be declared outside its parent, with the full type and name (Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets, vnet1/default), or inside the parent's resources array with one segment each (subnets, default), at any depth. A child declared inside is read as a top-level resource whose type and name carry its parent's, right after the parent, so template order creates the parent first. As in Azure, it does not depend on its parent unless its dependsOn says so, and it is never sent as part of the parent's body.

docs.title: Copy loops
docs.text:
All four kinds of copy loop are served, with copyIndex([loopName], [offset]):

  • Resources: "copy": {"name", "count", "mode", "batchSize"} deploys one resource per iteration. A dependsOn entry naming the loop depends on every instance, and a loop whose count is 0 deploys nothing and satisfies any dependency on it. Instances are created one at a time in iteration order, which meets both parallel and serial mode.
  • Properties: a copy array of {"name", "count", "input"} in a top-level resource's properties builds the array property of that name; copyIndex there names its loop.
  • Variables: a copy array in variables defines one array variable per entry, and a copy array inside a variable's value builds an array property of it.
  • Outputs: an output with "copy": {"count", "input"} is the array of its iterations.

A count is an integer from 0 to 800, as in Azure; anything else is InvalidTemplate. Loops nested in one another share one budget per template: once all of a template's copy iterations together pass 800 x 800, the template is an InvalidTemplate before the values are built. Azure caps the expanded template at 4 MB, which a deeper expansion could not fit in.

docs.title: Template functions
docs.text:
Group Functions Scope parameters, variables, resourceGroup, subscription, tenant, deployment, environment Resource ids resourceId (every arity), subscriptionResourceId, tenantResourceId, extensionResourceId Live reference (by name or id, optional api-version and 'Full'), every list* function (listKeys, ...) Loops copyIndex Logical true, false, null, not, and, or, if, bool, coalesce Comparison equals, less, lessOrEquals, greater, greaterOrEquals String concat, format, uniqueString, guid, newGuid, toLower, toUpper, string, int, float, json, length, empty, first, last, take, skip, split, replace, substring, trim, padLeft, startsWith, endsWith, contains, indexOf, lastIndexOf, like Encoding base64, base64ToString, base64ToJson, dataUri, dataUriToString, uri, uriComponent, uriComponentToString Array and object union, intersection, createArray, createObject, items, objectKeys, shallowMerge, tryGet, indexFromEnd, tryIndexFromEnd, distinct, join, array, range Numeric add, sub, mul, div, mod, min, max Date utcNow, dateTimeAdd, dateTimeFromEpoch, dateTimeToEpoch

environment() returns the subscription's cloud's own metadata (Azure's endpoints and suffixes), so a template that builds a hostname from environment().suffixes.storage gets the real Azure suffix, which the emulator routes.

docs.title: User-defined functions
docs.text: A template's functions section declares functions called as namespace.member(...). Each one is its output expression over its own parameters, checked against their declared types, and its result is checked against the output's type. The scope functions (resourceGroup(), subscription(), tenant(), deployment(), environment()) answer for the deployment. The restrictions Azure documents are each 400 InvalidTemplate: a function reads only its own parameters, never the template's or variables(), calls no other user-defined function, uses neither reference() nor a list* function, and declares no parameter defaults. An outer-scope nested deployment calls its parent's functions.

docs.title: Not supported yet
docs.text:
Each of these is refused with 400 InvalidTemplate, never skipped:

  • symbolic resource names (languageVersion 2.0)
  • a copy loop on a child declared inside its parent, and children inside a parent that has a copy loop: as the ARM docs advise, declare such children outside the parent, with the parent's name in theirs
  • the lambda functions (filter, map, reduce, sort, toObject, groupBy, mapValues), the CIDR functions, pickZones, providers, references, managementGroup, deployer, roleDefinitions
  • Key Vault parameter references
  • Complete mode, refused with 400 DeploymentModeNotSupported rather than run as Incremental

Deployments at management-group scope answer 404, and a nested deployment that targets a management group is 400 InvalidTemplate.

docs.title: Intentional deviations
docs.text:
• Retry-After: 1 on the PUT and on every status that is not final yet: Azure sends none, and clients then fall back to their own, much longer, poll interval (30 seconds for the az CLI, which polls once straight after the PUT); a local deployment usually finishes within the first second.
  • A refused cancel (of a deployment that is no longer running) is 409 DeploymentNotActive; Azure documents that only an Accepted or Running deployment can be canceled, but not the error.
  • Delete answers 204 at once; Azure answers 202 and lets the client poll.
  • whatIf answers 200 with the result at once, one of the two answers the spec declares; Azure answers 202 and lets the client poll a Location. An array that changed is one Modify of the whole array, where Azure lists its element changes as Array children, and a nested deployment's own changes are not predicted.
  • The first failing resource stops the deployment. Azure goes on with the resources that do not depend on it.
  • templateHash is a 64-bit hash of the minified, uppercased template, so it is the same for a deployment and for calculateTemplateHash of the same template whatever its whitespace or casing, which is what azd compares to skip an unchanged deployment. Azure does not publish its algorithm, so the value differs from Azure's.
  • uniqueString and guid have Azure's length and form but not its values: uniqueString is 13 lowercase base32 characters from a SHA-256 hash, guid a name-based UUID. A template that only needs stable unique names works; one that compares against a value computed in Azure does not.
  • format and the date functions support {n}, {n,width} and the N, D and X number formats, and the u, d, s and o date formats with the common custom tokens; any other format string is an InvalidTemplate rather than a guess.
  • if, and and or short-circuit, so a reference() in a branch the condition excludes is never sent.
  • Validation messages start with Azure's Deployment template validation failed: and use its codes, but the wording after it is floci-az's.
  • Deployments live in memory, as the rest of ARM state does.

docs.title: Azure Communication Services: Email
docs.text:
Compatible with the azure-communication-email SDK, the Microsoft.Communication ARM management plane, and any HTTP client. Floci AZ emulates the ACS Email data plane (POST /emails:send plus status polling) and captures every message in-memory for local inspection: a Mailpit-style mailbox for your tests. No real email is ever delivered.

HTTP-only: no Docker. Sending, status polling, inspection, and ARM resources are all in-process. There is no sidecar.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Send email: POST /emails:send accepts the full ACS payload (senderAddress, content with subject/plainText/html, recipients to/cc/bcc, attachments, replyTo, headers) and returns 202 Accepted with Operation-Location and Retry-After headers for polling. A caller-supplied Operation-Id request header is adopted as the operation id; without one the emulator generates a UUID, matching ACS
  • Operation status: GET /emails/operations/{operationId} reports the long-running operation status as {"id":…,"status":…,"error":null}, the same shape ACS returns. The emulator completes immediately, so the status is Succeeded
  • Inspection mailbox: GET /emailMessages lists every captured message, GET /emailMessages/{operationId} returns one in full (including the original request body), and DELETE /emailMessages clears the mailbox
  • ARM management plane: Microsoft.Communication/communicationServices, .../emailServices, and .../emailServices/{name}/domains/{domain} CreateOrUpdate, Get, Delete, and List, plus checkNameAvailability for communication service names

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
POST   /emails:send                              # data-plane send → 202 + Operation-Location
GET    /emails/operations/{operationId}          # operation status (Succeeded)

GET    /emailMessages                            # list captured messages
GET    /emailMessages/{operationId}              # single captured message detail
DELETE /emailMessages                            # clear the mailbox

PUT/GET/DELETE .../providers/Microsoft.Communication/communicationServices/{name}
PUT/GET/DELETE .../providers/Microsoft.Communication/emailServices/{name}
PUT/GET/DELETE .../providers/Microsoft.Communication/emailServices/{name}/domains/{domain}
POST   /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Communication/checkNameAvailability

The send and polling paths are also served when the SDK targets the ACS host form https://{resource}.communication.azure.com (use FLOCI_AZ_HOSTNAME/your hosts file to point that name at the emulator), or via the path-style /{account}-email/ suffix.

docs.title: Send an email (Python SDK)
docs.text:
from azure.communication.email import EmailClient

# In dev mode the access key is not validated
client = EmailClient.from_connection_string(
    "endpoint=http://localhost:4577/;accesskey=<any-base64-key>")

poller = client.begin_send({
    "senderAddress": "DoNotReply@example.com",
    "content": {"subject": "Hello", "plainText": "Hi from floci-az!"},
    "recipients": {"to": [{"address": "dev@example.com"}]},
})
result = poller.result()
print(result["id"], result["status"])   # operationId, Succeeded

docs.title: Send with curl
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:4577/emails:send?api-version=2023-03-31" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "senderAddress": "DoNotReply@example.com",
    "content": {"subject": "Hello", "plainText": "Hi!"},
    "recipients": {"to": [{"address": "dev@example.com"}]}
  }'
# → 202 Accepted, Operation-Location: .../emails/operations/{operationId}

docs.title: Inspect the captured mailbox
docs.text:
# List everything that was "sent"
curl -s "http://localhost:4577/emailMessages"
# → {"value":[{"operationId":"...","status":"Succeeded","subject":"Hello","toCount":1, ...}], "count":1}

# Fetch one message in full (includes the original request body)
curl -s "http://localhost:4577/emailMessages/<operationId>"

# Clear the mailbox between tests
curl -s -X DELETE "http://localhost:4577/emailMessages"

This makes it easy to assert in tests that your code sent the right subject, recipients, and body, without an SMTP server or a real ACS resource.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
floci-az:
  services:
    email:
      enabled: true
Env var Default Description FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_EMAIL_ENABLED true Enable/disable the service

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• No delivery. Messages are captured, never sent: nothing goes out over SMTP and no external recipient receives anything. The mailbox and the ARM resources are kept in the email storage backend, so they follow floci-az.storage.services.email.mode (the global storage.mode by default, memory unless set).
  • Operations always succeed immediately. There is no Running→Succeeded transition delay and no failure simulation. Retry-After: 3 is still returned on the 202 to match ACS, but the first poll already reports Succeeded.
  • Auth is permissive. The connection-string access key and Authorization header are accepted but not validated (dev mode), matching the rest of the emulator.
  • ARM resources are state-only. communicationServices/emailServices/domains return Succeeded provisioning state with synthesized properties (hostName, dataLocation); domain verification (SPF/DKIM TXT records) is not emulated.
  • Communication service names are global. A communication service owns {name}.communication.azure.com: the first subscription to create a name owns it, a create of the same name from another subscription or resource group answers 409 Conflict, and the name is free again once the owner deletes it. checkNameAvailability answers from the same owners, in any subscription, with the reasons and messages of the spec examples (AlreadyExists, NameAvailable), and answers Invalid for a name outside the communication service name rule (1 to 63 letters, digits, underscores and hyphens); a body whose type names another resource type is always available. Email services and domains are scoped to their resource group. A path that differs from the creating one only in case addresses the same resource, which keeps the casing of its first PUT.

docs.title: Microsoft Entra ID
docs.text:
A local OpenID Connect provider that issues real RS256-signed JWTs with a published discovery document and JWKS. This replaces the previous static, unsigned-token stub so apps that acquire and validate Entra tokens can work fully offline.

Phase 1 delivered the OIDC foundation and the two non-interactive grants (client credentials and resource-owner password / ROPC). Phase 2 (#120) adds the authorization code + PKCE grant for interactive (browser SPA) sign-in, plus a narrow Microsoft Graph slice for group membership. App registrations and their client secrets are managed through that slice too: see services/graph.md. Full Graph CRUD is not implemented.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Signed tokens: RS256 JWTs with a stable signing key persisted across restarts; app-only tokens carry idtyp=app, user access tokens name the user (upn and unique_name in v1.0, preferred_username in v2.0), and every token carries a unique uti, matching real Entra
  • Discovery: /.well-known/openid-configuration derived from the request base URL. It advertises only what the emulator serves, see Discovery document
  • JWKS: /discovery/v2.0/keys exposing the public signing key (kty, use, alg, kid, n, e) plus the self-signed cert chain (x5c, x5t)
  • Grants: client_credentials, password (ROPC), and authorization_code (auth code + PKCE), v1.0 and v2.0 token shapes; refresh_token at the v2.0 token endpoint
  • Azure-shaped errors: token errors return error, error_description (with the AADSTS code), error_codes, trace_id, correlation_id, timestamp, and error_uri
  • Dev seed: a default tenant, a well-known dev app registration, a dev user and a dev group
  • Permissive client authentication by default: client secrets are not checked, so any client_id and client_secret get a token and ClientSecretCredential works with zero setup. Set validate-client-credentials: true to check them against the directory (see Client credential validation)

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints are tenant-rooted at the base URL (port 4577). {tenant} may be a tenant id or common / organizations / consumers.

Path Purpose GET /{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize Authorize endpoint (auth code + PKCE) POST /{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token Token endpoint (v2.0) POST /{tenant}/oauth2/token Token endpoint (v1.0) GET /{tenant}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration OpenID discovery GET /{tenant}/.well-known/openid-configuration OpenID discovery GET /oidc/userinfo, POST /oidc/userinfo Scoped profile for a locally signed delegated access token GET /{tenant}/discovery/v2.0/keys JWKS GET /common/userrealm/{username}?api-version=1.0 Home realm discovery: always account_type: Managed, so MSAL username-password sign-in goes straight to the password grant

docs.title: Discovery document
docs.text:
GET /{tenant}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration lists only the grants, endpoints and response types the emulator implements, so a client that configures itself from discovery fails early with a clear message instead of calling a route that does not exist:

Field Value issuer The configured issuer, or {base}/{tenant}/v2.0 when unset (common stays common) authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, jwks_uri the routes in the table above grant_types_supported authorization_code, client_credentials, password, refresh_token response_types_supported code response_modes_supported query, fragment scopes_supported openid, profile, email, offline_access end_session_endpoint {base}/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/logout

There is no device_authorization_endpoint and the device code grant is not listed, because it is not implemented yet. msal-python's initiate_device_flow therefore stops with "You need to provide device authorization endpoint" before sending any request. end_session_endpoint is listed even though logout is not served yet, because MSAL.js refuses to log out without it.

When FLOCI_AZ_SERVICES_ENTRA_ISSUER is set, discovery and issued tokens use that same issuer, regardless of the hostname used to fetch discovery. This supports clients reaching Floci-AZ through different host and Docker addresses. Endpoint URLs still use the request base URL so the caller can reach them. Without an override, discovery keeps its request-derived issuer.

docs.title: Default tenant & dev credentials
docs.text: Value Default Tenant id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002 Client id 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 Client secret floci-az-dev-secret (checked only when validate-client-credentials is on) Dev user (UPN) dev-user@floci-az.local Dev group floci-az dev group (the dev user is a direct member)

docs.title: Interactive sign-in (authorization code + PKCE)
docs.text:
There is no real interactive consent screen: GET /{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize auto-approves against the seeded dev user (or a different seeded user, selected via login_hint) and redirects straight back to redirect_uri with a code: no login form, nothing to click through. This keeps the flow fully scriptable while still exercising the real auth-code+PKCE wire protocol that MSAL (@azure/msal-browser, @azure/msal-react, @azure/msal-node) speaks.

GET /{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize
    ?client_id=11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
    &redirect_uri=https://app.local/callback
    &response_type=code
    &response_mode=query          # or "fragment"
    &scope=openid profile
    &state=...
    &nonce=...
    &code_challenge=...           # PKCE S256 challenge
    &code_challenge_method=S256
    &login_hint=dev-user@floci-az.local   # optional; defaults to the seeded dev user

302s to {redirect_uri}?code=...&state=... (or #code=...&state=... for response_mode=fragment). The issued code is bound to the tenant, client_id, and redirect_uri from this request: redemption must repeat the same client_id/redirect_uri and happen against the same tenant, or it fails with invalid_grant. Redeem the code with grant_type=authorization_code:

curl -s http://localhost:4577/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002/oauth2/v2.0/token \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d client_id=11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 \
  -d redirect_uri=https://app.local/callback \
  -d code=<code from the redirect> \
  -d code_verifier=<the PKCE verifier for the challenge you sent>

The response carries an access_token, plus an id_token when openid was requested. The ID token's aud is always the client id (per OIDC, regardless of v1.0/v2.0), and it echoes the nonce from the /authorize request: MSAL rejects an ID token whose nonce doesn't match. PKCE verification (S256 or plain) is skipped when /authorize was called without a code_challenge: client_id is still required and bound to the code, so an omitted challenge no longer hands a usable code to a caller who doesn't know the client. There is no app-registration redirect-URI allow-list yet, so any client_id is accepted at /authorize, matching this phase's permissive client validation elsewhere (client_credentials is likewise accepted without strict validation).

docs.title: Refreshing a session
docs.text:
Include offline_access in the original authorization request to receive an opaque refresh_token from the v2.0 code exchange. A request without this scope does not receive one. Renew the session without another authorization request:

curl -s http://localhost:4577/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002/oauth2/v2.0/token \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d client_id=11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 \
  --data-urlencode 'refresh_token=<refresh token from the code exchange>'

Send the client's secret too when the session used a confidential client and credential validation is enabled. HTTP Basic and form credentials follow the same policy as other grants. A code exchange that supplies a secret or assertion, or uses a registered web.redirectUris entry, binds a confidential session. Public-client sessions need no secret.

The response contains a fresh access token and replacement refresh token. openid permits a fresh ID token for the same user, without repeating the authorization request's nonce. MSAL's client_info=1 is supported for account caching. An optional scope selects the access token's scopes, including another resource such as Graph after an ARM sign-in. The emulator does not model consent, so additional scopes are accepted for the same client and user session. Omitting scope uses the original authorization scopes, even after a replacement was issued for a different resource. A narrowed access token does not remove those default scopes.

Refresh tokens last 90 days by default, and a replacement starts a new 90-day lifetime. A redirect URI registered under the application's spa.redirectUris instead creates a 24-hour session; all replacements retain that original deadline. Replacement does not revoke the old token, matching Microsoft's refresh-token contract.

Tokens remain bound to the client and resolved tenant that authorized them, and renewal resolves the same user in that directory. Invalid, revoked, expired or incorrectly bound tokens return invalid_grant. Expiry uses AADSTS700082, or AADSTS700084 for the fixed SPA lifetime. Refresh state uses the existing Entra storage mode and persists only token digests. Issuance removes expired records at most once a minute, including on the first issuance after restart. Emulator reset clears all refresh state. Cross-tenant consent, B2B sessions, password-change revocation and Graph's revokeSignInSessions action are not modelled. The v1.0 refresh grant is not implemented.

Group membership for the signed-in user is not embedded in the token (no groups claim, matching real Entra's default behavior): call the Graph getMemberGroups endpoint instead, see services/graph.md.

docs.title: Acquiring a token
docs.text:
Pythoncurl 
from azure.identity import ClientSecretCredential

cred = ClientSecretCredential(
    tenant_id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
    client_id="11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
    client_secret="floci-az-dev-secret",  # any value works unless validate-client-credentials is on
    authority="http://localhost:4577",
)
token = cred.get_token("api://resource/.default")
print(token.token)  # RS256-signed JWT

curl -s http://localhost:4577/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002/oauth2/v2.0/token \
  -d grant_type=client_credentials \
  -d client_id=11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 \
  -d client_secret=floci-az-dev-secret \
  -d scope=api://resource/.default

docs.title: Validating a token
docs.text:
Fetch the JWKS and validate the signature, iss, aud, and exp:

import jwt
from jwt import PyJWKClient

jwks = PyJWKClient("http://localhost:4577/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002/discovery/v2.0/keys")
signing_key = jwks.get_signing_key_from_jwt(token)
claims = jwt.decode(token, signing_key.key, algorithms=["RS256"], audience="api://resource")

docs.title: Client credential validation
docs.text:
By default the token endpoint accepts any client: an unregistered client_id and a wrong secret both get a token, and the first unregistered client_id is logged once at WARN. With validate-client-credentials: true the client is checked against the directory instead:

Request Response a client_id not registered in the tenant 400 unauthorized_client, AADSTS700016 a secret that matches none of the app's secrets, or one before its startDateTime 401 invalid_client, AADSTS7000215 a secret that matches but is past its endDateTime 401 invalid_client, AADSTS7000222 client_credentials with neither a secret nor a client_assertion 401 invalid_client, AADSTS7000218 no client_id at all 400 invalid_request, AADSTS900144
